# Cwift.net

> Cwift.net is the minimal, first-person site for Brian Ward's 24-hour desktop appraisals of California homes and condominiums. Brian Ward is a California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser (license AR036053) who has appraised California homes since 2004. Reports are emailed within 24 hours of payment and photos, seven days a week. Same appraiser and service as cwift.com; standard-schedule reports are also offered by date-of-death.com.

## Facts
- Within 24 hours: Standard Desktop $675, Basic Desktop $450
- Regular schedule (5–10 business days): Standard $449, Basic $299
- The 24 hours start once payment and photos have both arrived; weekends and holidays count
- Coverage: all of California, every county and ZIP code (207 county, city and neighborhood pages at https://www.cwift.net/areas); single-family homes, condominiums and townhomes (not 2–4 units, apartments, commercial or land); not for loans
- Also called: a virtual, remote or online appraisal; it is a full appraisal by a licensed appraiser without a site visit
- Contact: contact@cwift.net or https://www.cwift.net/order. Phone (call or text): (619) 491-7071. Email and online submission are the fastest way to get service
- Statement: I've prepared desktop appraisals for every purpose on this list. Some situations still call for an in-person appraisal, though, so check with your attorney or tax advisor first to make sure a desktop report is right for yours.

## Uses (date of death first)
- [Date of death & step-up in basis](https://www.cwift.net/uses#date-of-death): Heirs usually receive a fresh tax basis equal to the home's value on the day the owner died. The appraisal pins down that figure, so capital gains are calculated correctly when the house sells, even if the death was years ago.
- [Trusts & estates](https://www.cwift.net/uses#trust-estate): Trustees and executors need a value they can defend: for an accounting, for dividing things fairly, or for selling the house to one of the beneficiaries. A signed appraisal answers the question of where the number came from.
- [Divorce & separation](https://www.cwift.net/uses#divorce): Whether one of you keeps the house or it gets sold, settlement talks move faster with an independent value. I can value the home as of today, the date of separation, or both.
- [Family sales & buyouts](https://www.cwift.net/uses#family-transfers): Buying out a brother's share, selling to your daughter, or splitting a house with a former partner? The appraisal gives everyone the same starting point and records a fair price.
- [Gift tax](https://www.cwift.net/uses#gift-tax): Deeding a house, or part of one, to a relative is a gift with a value that gets reported. The appraisal supports the figure on the federal gift-tax return, Form 709.
- [Prop 19 transfers](https://www.cwift.net/uses#prop-19): When a parent's home passes to a child, Prop 19 limits how much of the old assessment carries over. Market value on the transfer date shows where you stand with the county assessor.
- [Property tax appeals](https://www.cwift.net/uses#property-tax-appeal): If the county assesses your home above what it would sell for, an independent appraisal is the evidence for a decline-in-value review or a formal appeal.
- [Bankruptcy](https://www.cwift.net/uses#bankruptcy): Your attorney needs a supportable value for the schedules and the homestead exemption. Problems with the house get documented from your photos, so they count.
- [Before you sell](https://www.cwift.net/uses#pre-listing): Set the asking price with an opinion from someone who isn't trying to win your listing.
- [Before you buy](https://www.cwift.net/uses#pre-purchase): Paying cash, buying from family, or skipping the appraisal contingency? Check the price while you can still walk away.
- [Immigration sponsors (I-864)](https://www.cwift.net/uses#immigration): Sponsors who count home equity on the Affidavit of Support are asked for a recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser. This is that appraisal.
- [Bail & property bonds](https://www.cwift.net/uses#bail-bonds): Courts that take a property bond want proof of the equity, usually from a licensed appraiser. A current report keeps the bond paperwork moving.

## Questions

Q: How fast is 24 hours, really?
A: Your report is emailed no more than 24 hours after I have both your payment and your photos. Saturdays, Sundays and holidays count like any other day.

Q: What do I need to send?
A: The address, what the appraisal is for, the date you need the value for, and photos of the outside and inside. A few lines about recent updates or problems help too.

Q: Do you come out to the house?
A: No. That's what makes it a desktop appraisal, and it's why it can be finished in a day.

Q: Will my CPA, attorney or the IRS accept it?
A: It's a signed appraisal by a California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, prepared under USPAP, the national appraisal standards. I've done desktop appraisals for every purpose on this site, but acceptance is up to whoever receives the report, so check with your advisor if you're unsure.

Q: Can you value a date in the past?
A: Yes. Most date-of-death, divorce and gift appraisals are for past dates. If the house has changed since then, send older photos or describe what's different.

Q: What does it cost?
A: Within 24 hours: $675 for a Standard Desktop or $450 for a Basic Desktop. On the regular 5–10 business-day schedule they're $449 and $299.

Q: Standard or Basic?
A: Both use the same analysis. Standard adds photos, maps, a property description and a market section, which helps when someone else will review the report.

Q: Why can't I call?
A: Because it would slow things down. Email and the form put everything in writing at once, photos included. Write to contact@cwift.net any time.

Q: How do I pay?
A: You'll get a secure invoice by email after I've reviewed your request.

Q: Which properties can you appraise?
A: Single-family homes and condominiums, including townhomes, anywhere in California. Not 2–4 unit buildings, apartment buildings, commercial property or land.

Q: Can I use it to refinance or get a loan?
A: No. Lenders order their own appraisals.

Q: What if the report gets something wrong about my house?
A: Tell me. If I misread a feature or the condition, I'll correct it at no charge.

Q: How much is my house worth?
A: That's exactly what an appraisal answers. I study recent sales of similar homes nearby, adjust for the differences, and give you a signed opinion of market value, as of today or any past date you need.

Q: My mom passed away. What value do I need for her house?
A: Usually its market value on the date she died, because that's generally the heirs' new tax basis. Your tax preparer will confirm. I can value that date even if it was years ago.

Q: Can my spouse and I use the same appraiser?
A: Yes. I often work for both spouses at once, once both sides have signed off on the date and the photos. That gives you one number to negotiate from instead of two competing ones.

Q: Can you value the house as if the repairs were finished?
A: Often, yes. Tell me what work is planned when you order, and I'll confirm whether I can do it and how the report will describe it before you're invoiced.

Q: Do I need an appraisal to appeal my property taxes?
A: It isn't required, but an independent appraisal of the January 1 value is strong evidence for a Prop 8 review with the assessor or a formal appeal to the county board.

Q: Can I use my house for a property bond?
A: Often. Under Penal Code §1298 the court has to find equity of at least twice the bail, and most courts want a licensed appraiser's report in the bond packet. Check your court's instructions first.

Q: Can we skip the probate referee?
A: Sometimes. A court can waive the referee for good cause under Probate Code §8903, and then an independent appraisal can supply the value for the inventory. Ask your probate attorney whether it's realistic in your case.

Q: What if I'm donating the house to a charity?
A: Then a different set of IRS rules applies: a qualified appraisal timed around the donation and a signed Form 8283. Ask me before ordering and I'll tell you whether my report fits.

Q: Is a virtual or online appraisal the same thing?
A: If a licensed appraiser signs it, a virtual or remote appraisal is what I call a desktop appraisal. An instant online estimate isn't an appraisal at all.

Q: Do you appraise homes in my city?
A: If it's in California, yes: every county and every ZIP code, at the same fee. The areas page lists the counties, cities and neighborhoods I've written about, but I'm not limited to them.


## Uses in detail

### Date of death & step-up in basis: After a death: what was the house worth that day?
When someone dies, the house generally gets a fresh tax basis for the heirs: its market value on the date of death. That single number decides how much gain, if any, shows up when the house is sold. I value the home as of that day, using sales from around that time and whatever photos you have from then: family snapshots, old listing pictures, insurance photos.
Some estates also need the figure for a federal estate tax return, Form 706. Only very large estates owe that tax (the 2026 exclusion is $15 million per person), but a surviving spouse sometimes files the return anyway to keep the unused exemption, a step called portability. The executor can also choose the alternate valuation date, six months after death, on that return. California has no estate tax of its own.
If the house was cleaned out, painted or remodeled since, tell me what changed. The value is for the house as it stood on the date of death, not as it looks now.

### Trusts & estates: Settling a trust or a probate estate
Trustees and executors need a value they can explain to the family, the CPA and sometimes the court. I appraise the home for the trust's records, for evening out shares when one beneficiary keeps the house, for a sale to a family member, for setting a list price, and for the beneficiaries' tax basis.
In a formal probate, the court's probate referee normally values the real estate for the inventory. Families still order my report alongside the referee's figure when their CPA wants the full reasoning behind the basis.
A personal representative may also petition to skip the referee for good cause under Probate Code §8903. The petition includes a proposed inventory with values, the hearing is at least 15 days later, and the referee can object. If the judge grants it, an independent appraisal can carry the real estate value. Your probate attorney will know whether that's worth trying.

### Divorce & separation: Divorce or separation: one number you can both work with
Whether one of you keeps the house or it gets sold, the settlement needs a value. I can value it as of today, the date of separation, or both.
Plenty of couples hire me together as one neutral appraiser. Both of you are named in the report, both attorneys agree on the valuation date and on the photos I'll rely on, and the report spells out what was agreed. If the house has slipped since the separation, valuing it as of the agreed date, from photos taken then, keeps that out of the number.
If one of you lives there and won't allow a visit, that's rarely an obstacle for a desktop appraisal: public records, old listing photos and what you know about the house are usually enough, and I state in the report what I relied on. Desktop reports suit mediation and negotiated buyouts. If your case is headed to trial, ask your attorney whether an inspected appraisal with testimony would serve you better.

### Family sales & buyouts: Selling to family or buying out a co-owner
Buying out a sibling's share of an inherited house, selling to your daughter, or untangling a house you own with a former partner are all easier when the whole family works from one independent number.
A documented price matters later, too. When a sale inside the family is below market value, the difference can count as a gift for federal tax purposes, and the appraisal shows what market value was.

### Gift tax: Giving a house, or part of one
If you deed a house, or a share of one, to a relative or a trust, the IRS wants what it was worth that day reported on the federal gift-tax return, Form 709. My appraisal supports that figure, and I can value a gift made months ago as of the date of the deed.
Giving a fractional share? I value the house itself; any discount for the partial interest is a separate analysis, usually by a business valuation specialist. The same goes when the gift is a stake in a family LLC or partnership that holds the house. The specialist starts from the property's market value, then takes off whatever discount fits a minority share that can't force a sale and can't easily be sold.
Donating a house to a charity is different. It's an income-tax deduction, and for real estate claimed above $5,000 the IRS wants a qualified appraisal made within the 60 days before the gift or after it, by the return's due date, with the appraiser signing off on Form 8283. Tell me the donation date and I'll tell you before you pay whether a desktop report fits.

### Prop 19 transfers: Inheriting a parent's home: what happens to the property tax
Since February 16, 2021, Prop 19 lets a child keep part of a parent's low assessment only if the child makes the home their main residence, and only up to a cap that adjusts every two years. The home's market value on the transfer date decides how much of the old assessment carries over.
I give you that value so you can decide whether to move in, rent the place out, sell it or buy out your siblings, and so you have evidence if the assessor's number looks high.

### Property tax appeals: Think your property taxes are too high?
If your home would have sold for less than its assessed value on January 1, you can ask the county assessor for a decline-in-value review under Prop 8. If the assessor won't budge, you can file a formal appeal with the county assessment appeals board. That window opens July 2 and closes September 15 in some counties and November 30 in most others.
An independent appraisal of the January 1 value is the kind of evidence those boards weigh. Photos of anything that hurts value, like an old roof, foundation cracks or a kitchen nobody has touched in decades, matter here, because the assessor's numbers rarely reflect what's inside.

### Bankruptcy: Bankruptcy: the value on the schedules
Your attorney needs a supportable value for the house on the bankruptcy schedules and for the homestead exemption, usually as of the filing date. Problems with the house get documented from your photos and repair bids, so they count in the value.
If the trustee or a creditor argues for a different number, your attorney may want an inspected appraisal and testimony; I do those through Brian Ward Appraisal in San Diego and Riverside Counties.

### Before you sell: Before you sell: set the price on evidence
An agent's suggested list price is partly a pitch for the listing. My opinion of value comes from someone with nothing riding on the sale, built from the sales a buyer's appraiser is likely to look at.
I can often value the house as if planned repairs were finished. Describe the work when you order, and I'll tell you whether that's possible, and how the report will say it, before you're invoiced.

### Before you buy: Before you buy: check the price while you can walk away
Cash buyers, family purchases and buyers who waived the appraisal contingency still want to know the price holds up. I work from the listing photos, your own photos from the showing and the disclosures, fast enough to fit inside a contingency period.
It's for your decision only; if you're borrowing, the lender orders its own appraisal.

### Immigration sponsors (I-864): Sponsoring a relative (Form I-864)
If your income falls short of the I-864 requirement, assets can make up the difference, and home equity is one of them. Equity here means what an appraiser says the house is worth, less everything owed on it, and the form's instructions ask for a recent report from a licensed appraiser.
Order close to the date you'll send the evidence, so the report is current. Your immigration attorney can tell you whether leaning on home equity makes sense in your case.

### Bail & property bonds: Using a house for bail
Under Penal Code §1298, a California court can accept the equity in a house in place of cash bail, as long as that equity is at least double the bail. Equity is what the house is worth, less the loans and liens against it.
Courts publish their own property-bond packets, and many ask for an appraisal by a licensed or certified appraiser, sometimes done within the last few months. Bail agents who take a house as collateral often want one too. Check what your court or agent needs, then order; the report comes back within a day of payment and photos.


## Why desktop appraisals are credible
1. The rulebook allows it: Appraisers follow USPAP, the national appraisal standards, and California requires licensed appraisers to comply. USPAP lets the appraiser decide how much inspection an assignment needs, and requires the report to say plainly whether the property was inspected. My desktop reports disclose that, along with what information I relied on.
2. Mortgage companies use them: Fannie Mae's Selling Guide (section B4-1.2-02) allows desktop appraisals, done without a current visit to the home or the comparable sales, for some home-purchase loans. If the method holds up when hundreds of thousands of dollars are being lent against a house, it holds up for an estate, a buyout or a tax return.
3. The IRS list doesn't include a visit: For gift-tax returns, Treasury regulations spell out who may prepare a supporting appraisal and what it has to contain: dates, a description of the property, the method, the information considered and the reasoning. Walking through the house isn't on the list (26 CFR 301.6501(c)-1(f)(3)).
4. Every appraisal is mostly remote: Appraisers judge comparable sales from MLS records, photos and public data without ever going inside them. In a desktop appraisal your home is studied the same way, with better photos, because you took them.
5. Your evidence covers more: A quick walk-through can miss the new roof, the old water damage or the bathroom that hasn't been touched since 1978. Your photos and notes can show all of it, and the report lists what was provided.
6. Someone stands behind it: Every report is signed by me, Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, license AR036053. You can look the license up on the state's appraiser search. I keep a workfile for every report, and if I misread something about your home I fix it free.


## Area pages

### Alameda County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/alameda-county)
County seat: Oakland. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: September 15. Across Alameda County I keep comparables on your side of the hills. A Piedmont Tudor, a San Lorenzo tract house, a Fremont townhouse and a Sunol ranch on acreage each sell in a market of their own.
ZIP codes: 49 ZIP codes
Alameda County runs from the Oakland and Berkeley flats into the hills, out to the island city of Alameda, down the bay to Fremont and over the ridge to Livermore. I value homes here on short notice after a parent dies, in a divorce or before a sibling buyout, and in this county a street of shingled bungalows can be a world away from a 1990s cul-de-sac.
- On Alameda island, East End Victorians sit a short drive from the lagoon-front houses of the South Shore and Bay Farm Island, so I match era and lagoon frontage first.
- In the Oakland hills a bay view, a long stair from the street, or a rebuild after the 1991 fire can outweigh an extra bedroom, so I compare sales on similar slopes.
- Over the ridge in Livermore, Pleasanton and Dublin, I'm mostly comparing tract homes built from the 1960s on, where floor plan, HOA and freeway noise carry the weight.
Photos: In the hills, photograph the view from your main rooms and the climb from the street. In the older flats of Oakland, Alameda and San Leandro, show the basement or crawlspace and any visible foundation bolting.
Q: Do I need my own appraisal for probate in Alameda County?
A: Not always. A probate referee values the estate's assets for the court, and my report doesn't replace that. Executors from Oakland to Livermore still hire me for an independent date-of-death value to support the step-up in basis or settle a buyout.
Q: Our Oakland condo is assessed above what it would sell for, can an appraisal help?
A: It can. If you bought near a peak, the assessor can lower the assessment while the market is down, and my report shows sales from your building as of January 1. Alameda County's 2026 appeal deadline was September 15.

### Alpine County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/alpine-county)
County seat: Markleeville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: September 15. Across Alpine County I move between ski-area cabins at Kirkwood and Bear Valley, older homes in Markleeville and Woodfords, and the high meadows along the Carson River. Snow and access differ in each, so I keep comparables close.
ZIP codes: 96120
Alpine County has more mountain than houses, and I feel it the moment I start looking for sales. Homes here are cabins near the ski lifts, small places around Markleeville and Woodfords, and older homes along the Carson River. When a parent's cabin passes to the kids, or a divorce decides who keeps it, you need a clear value fast.
- Sales here are few, so I reach to Kirkwood, Bear Valley and nearby mountain towns when needed, and I explain each adjustment for snow, road access and distance to the lifts.
- I check whether your cabin sits on a road that's plowed all winter or past the closure gates on Ebbetts or Monitor Pass. Year-round access usually sells more easily.
- Nearly all of the county is public land, so I look at what your parcel actually borders, whether national forest, meadow, river or a neighbor, using the parcel map and your photos.
Photos: Show me the roofline and any snow shed over the doors, the wood stove or propane heat, the road out front and the view from the deck. Winter shots you already have help too.
Q: Can you appraise our Alpine County cabin in winter when it's snowed in?
A: Yes. Nobody has to shovel a path or wait for the passes to open. Summer photos you already have, plus a few fresh ones if you can reach the door, are enough, and I note the season in the report.
Q: We inherited Dad's Markleeville cabin, but none of us live in California. Now what?
A: No one needs to fly in. One of you, a neighbor or the caretaker can send photos, and I pull the county record and nearby mountain sales. Everyone gets the same report by email, so you can decide together whether to keep or sell.

### Amador County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/amador-county)
County seat: Jackson. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Amador County climbs from oak grassland near Lake Camanche through the Highway 49 towns and Shenandoah Valley vineyards to snow country toward Kirkwood. I compare each Amador home with sales at its own elevation and setting.
ZIP codes: 95629, 95640, 95642, 95665, 95666, 95669, 95685, 95689
Amador County homes run from gold-rush houses on the hills of Sutter Creek and Jackson to ranch houses among the oaks near Ione and cabins in the pines at Pioneer. Amador requests usually reach me after a parent dies, during a divorce, or when a son or daughter moving into the family house needs a number fast.
- Old homes in Sutter Creek, Jackson and Amador City can sit on stone or brick foundations, with additions from several eras. I sort out what's original and how the add-ons were built.
- Around Plymouth and Fiddletown, homes with vineyard views or a few acres of vines sell in a different market than in-town houses, so I compare them with other wine-country sales.
- Up Highway 88 at Pine Grove and Pioneer, elevation changes the picture: snow, pines, wood heat and propane. I compare those homes with each other, not with sales down around Ione.
Photos: Photograph the foundation where you can see it, the porch and old additions, the wood stove, and the well and septic area. On acreage, add the outbuildings, fencing and the view across the oaks or vines.
Q: Mom's house in Jackson is coming to me. Does Prop 19 change the taxes?
A: It can. Under Prop 19, a child who makes the Jackson house a primary home may keep all or part of the parent's tax base, depending on market value at the transfer. I give you that value; the Amador assessor and your tax advisor apply the rules.
Q: Should we sell our parents' Amador County house as is or fix it first?
A: That choice is yours. I appraise the house as it stands, sagging porch and original kitchen included, so you can weigh that number against repair bids and the months a fix-up takes. Along Highway 49, plenty of older homes sell without updates.

### Butte County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/butte-county)
County seat: Oroville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Butte County takes me from flat valley ground around Chico and Gridley, through oak foothills near Oroville, up into the pines on the Ridge. I draw sales from the same part of Butte County whenever I can.
ZIP codes: 16 ZIP codes
Butte County runs from the orchards around Chico and Gridley up to the Ridge and the foothills around Lake Oroville. I value bungalows in Chico's Avenues, ranch homes on almond acreage, older places in Oroville, and houses rebuilt after the Camp Fire. Calls come after a death, during a divorce, or near an appeal deadline, so the value can't wait.
- On the Ridge, many homes are new builds on lots the 2018 Camp Fire cleared. I compare a rebuild with other rebuilds, and an older survivor with older homes.
- Farm parcels near Durham, Gridley and Biggs often include a farmhouse, a shop and a well. I value the home on its homesite and flag land that needs a farm appraiser.
- Near the Feather River in Oroville and Thermalito, I check flood maps. In Chico's older neighborhoods, I look hard at foundations, wiring and how well a prewar house was updated.
Photos: Photograph the orchard or pasture from the house, the well and pump, and any shop. On the Ridge, show the cleared ground around the house; in an older Chico home, the woodwork and kitchen.
Q: When is the deadline to appeal our property taxes in Butte County this year?
A: For 2026, the deadline to file an assessment appeal in Butte County is November 30. A decline-in-value appeal looks at your home's worth on January 1, so I appraise it as of that date using Chico, Oroville or Ridge sales. I can't promise the outcome.
Q: How do I find out what my parents' house in Chico is worth?
A: Send me the Chico address and photos of every room, the outside and the yard. I check the county record and past listings, compare the house with sales from the same part of Chico, and value it as of today or the date your parent died.

### Calaveras County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/calaveras-county)
County seat: San Andreas. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. In Calaveras County I work from the grassland around New Hogan Lake up to the big pines above Arnold, treating Valley Springs, Copperopolis, the Highway 49 towns and the high country as separate markets.
ZIP codes: 95222, 95223, 95228, 95232, 95245, 95246, 95247, 95249, 95251, 95252, 95255, 95257
Calaveras County homes change with elevation, from ranch houses on oak acreage around Valley Springs and Copperopolis, to the old streets of Murphys and Angels Camp, to cabins under the pines in Arnold. An estate here usually needs a date-of-death value, and a divorce needs a number soon; I build both from your photos and the county's own records.
- Around Arnold and Dorrington, snow and pines set the market; around Valley Springs, oak acreage and wells do. I keep comparables at the same elevation, since those homes rarely compete.
- Homes on Lake Tulloch near Copperopolis and golf-course homes at Saddle Creek need sales from the same setting. I note dock rights, HOA rules and how close the water really is.
- Where the Butte Fire burned around Mountain Ranch and Mokelumne Hill, I look at rebuilt homes, cleared lots and surviving trees, and check the record for what stood there before.
Photos: Photograph the well head and pressure tank, the propane tank, cleared space around the house, and the data plate if it's a manufactured home. Lake homes: the dock and view. Arnold cabins: the roof and deck.
Q: Can you appraise Dad's Murphys house as of the day he died last year?
A: Yes. A date-of-death value for a Murphys house is a retrospective appraisal, and I do them often. I use Calaveras sales from around that date, county records, and photos from that time if you have them; current photos work if little has changed.
Q: Do a well and septic system hurt home value in Calaveras County?
A: Not by themselves. Rural Calaveras homes mostly run on wells and septic, so buyers expect them. I look at the well's output if you know it, the septic system's age, and whether the acreage is usable ground or steep oak hillside. Recent inspection reports help.

### Colusa County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/colusa-county)
County seat: Colusa. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Colusa County runs from the Sacramento River levees, across flat rice and orchard ground along I-5, to the dry Coast Range foothills around Stonyford. A river house and a hill place don't share a market, so I compare each with its own.
ZIP codes: 95912, 95932, 95970, 95979, 95987
Colusa County is rice country, with most homes in small towns like Colusa, Williams, Arbuckle and Maxwell or out on farm ground near the Sacramento River. I see older wood-frame houses in town and ranch homes on a few acres with a shop. When a parent dies and the heirs live far away, I can value a Colusa County house quickly from a neighbor's photos.

- Homes along the Sacramento River near Colusa, Grimes and Princeton sit behind levees. I check the flood maps and look at the foundation and grade in your photos.
- Out in rice and almond country, a home often comes with a well, septic and a shop. I credit the shop when buyers would pay for it and leave farm ground to farm appraisers.
Photos: Photograph the house from the road and the field side, the well and pressure tank, the shop and barns, and where the foundation meets the ground. In town, show the porch, floors and kitchen.
Q: I live out of state. Can you appraise my late mother's house in Colusa?
A: Yes. A neighbor, a relative or a Colusa agent can walk through with a phone and send me photos of every room and the outside. I pull the county record and past MLS history, compare with Colusa County sales, and email you the report.
Q: Are there enough home sales around Williams and Arbuckle for a reliable appraisal?
A: Fewer than around Chico or Woodland, so I widen the search across Colusa County and back in time, then adjust for size, condition, acreage and town versus country. The report explains each choice, so an heir or attorney anywhere can follow it.

### Contra Costa County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/contra-costa-county)
County seat: Martinez. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Contra Costa County holds very different markets: the Richmond flats, Lamorinda behind the tunnel, the 680 corridor under Mount Diablo, and East County's newer tracts and Delta waterfront. I compare your home only with its own corner of the county.
ZIP codes: 38 ZIP codes
Contra Costa County runs from Crockett and Martinez on the Carquinez Strait through Lamorinda and around Mount Diablo, then out Highway 4 to the Delta. I value homes here when someone needs a number fast, after a death, in a divorce or before a buyout, and one week can bring me a Rossmoor condo, an Orinda ranch and a Brentwood two-story with leased solar.
- In Lamorinda, lots are often steep and irregular, and a flat usable yard can matter as much as the house, so I read the parcel map alongside your yard photos.
- Along the 680 corridor, many Walnut Creek and Pleasant Hill homes are 1950s and 1960s ranches, and I sort them by how much has been updated.
- In Discovery Bay, a home whose dock has a quick run to open Delta water sells differently from one deep inside the channels, so I match water frontage before anything else.
Photos: Photograph the Mount Diablo view if you have one, the back yard's slope, and the solar panels with the lease or purchase papers. In Discovery Bay, show the dock, the boat lift and the water view.
Q: We live out of state, can you appraise Mom's house in Contra Costa County?
A: Yes. A neighbor or a cleaner can walk the house with a phone, whether it's in Pleasant Hill or Pittsburg, and send me every room, the roof line and the yard. I add county records and recent sales, and every heir gets the same report by email.
Q: How do you value a Rossmoor co-op or condo after a parent passes?
A: Rossmoor is a 55-plus community whose co-ops, condos and other homes are grouped into separate mutuals, and they don't trade like other Walnut Creek condos. I compare sales inside Rossmoor, matching the mutual, floor plan, view and updates.

### Del Norte County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/del-norte-county)
County seat: Crescent City. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Del Norte County is small but varied: coastal flats and lagoons around Crescent City and Fort Dick, river canyons along the Smith and Klamath, and steep forest up Highway 199. A town lot and Gasquet acreage sell differently, and I keep them apart.
ZIP codes: 95531, 95543, 95548, 95567
Del Norte County is the far northwest corner of California, and most homes are in and around Crescent City, with more in Fort Dick, Smith River, Hiouchi and Gasquet. Many are older wood-frame houses and manufactured homes that live with steady rain. When a parent dies or a marriage ends, I can value a Del Norte house quickly from your photos.
- Low-lying parts of Crescent City near the harbor sit in the mapped tsunami hazard area. I check the maps and compare those homes with others in the same zone when sales allow.
- Rain off the Pacific is hard on Crescent City houses. In your photos I look for moss on the roof, soft siding, worn decks and damp crawlspaces, and adjust for what I find.
- Rural places near Lake Earl, Fort Dick and along the Smith River often have wells, septic and outbuildings. I weigh river frontage and acreage against the county's few rural sales.
Photos: Photograph the roof up close, the siding on the weather side, the deck, and the crawlspace vents. Show the wood stove or heat source and the view toward the harbor, river or redwoods.
Q: Do I need a separate appraisal if Mom's Crescent City house is in probate?
A: In a Del Norte County probate, the court's probate referee values the house for the inventory. Executors here still often order an independent appraisal to price the house or document the date-of-death value. I value it as of the day she died with Crescent City sales.
Q: Will rain damage and an old roof hurt our home's value in Del Norte County?
A: That depends on how far the water has gotten. I value the house as it stands in this wet climate, so show me the roof, ceilings, siding and soft spots up close. I compare it with Crescent City area homes in similar shape and say plainly what I saw.

### El Dorado County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/el-dorado-county)
County seat: Placerville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. El Dorado County runs from the Folsom Lake edge of El Dorado Hills through oak foothills and apple orchards to the Tahoe basin. I treat the Highway 50 suburbs, the Georgetown Divide, the south county wine hills and the lake as separate markets.
ZIP codes: 19 ZIP codes
El Dorado County takes me from newer homes in El Dorado Hills and Cameron Park to older houses on Placerville's hills, apple country around Camino, and cabins near South Lake Tahoe. The work is most often a divorce, a parent's estate, or siblings deciding who keeps the house, and each needs a value both sides accept, fast.
- In Serrano and the other gated El Dorado Hills neighborhoods, I compare within the same community when I can, since dues, golf frontage and views set real differences.
- Cameron Park has an airpark where homes sit along taxiways with their own hangars. Those are a niche, so I look for other airpark sales before ordinary ones.
- Above Pollock Pines and around Grizzly Flats, I weigh snow, fire history and defensible space. Since the Caldor Fire, some parcels hold new homes and some only foundations; your photos show which.
Photos: Photograph the view off the back deck, the pool and yard, the roof and any solar, and the cleared space around the house. For a Tahoe cabin, add the steep driveway, parking pad and snow-load roof.
Q: We're divorcing and both want the El Dorado Hills house. Who sets the value?
A: Many El Dorado Hills couples agree on one neutral appraiser, and I'm glad to be that person. I value the house as of today or your date of separation, as your attorneys ask, using nearby sales, and both sides get the same report.
Q: Does vacation rental income count when you appraise a South Lake Tahoe cabin?
A: Not directly. I value the cabin by what similar Tahoe homes sold for. A rental permit can still matter, since the city and county limit where vacation rentals are allowed. Tell me whether yours has one, and I'll look for sales that match.

### Fresno County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/fresno-county)
County seat: Fresno. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Fresno County holds very different markets: valley farm country, dry west-side towns toward Interstate 5, oak foothills east of Clovis and Sierra cabins up Highway 168. I compare each house with sales from its own setting.
ZIP codes: 50 ZIP codes
Fresno County runs from vineyards and orchards around Selma, Reedley and Kingsburg through the oak foothills near Prather and Auberry to the cabins at Shaver Lake. I appraise farmhouses on acreage, small-town homes and west-side houses in Coalinga and Mendota. After a death or a divorce, you may be hours away, and I can work from photos someone takes for you.
- Rural parcels outside Sanger, Fowler and Kerman usually come with a well, septic and a shop or barn. I sort out what adds value to the home and compare with other rural homesites.
- At Shaver Lake and Huntington Lake, I check winter access, the roof and how close the lot came to the 2020 Creek Fire, and I compare with other mountain cabin sales.
- West of Highway 99, in Coalinga, Huron and Firebaugh, sales are thin. I widen the search carefully and explain why each comparable fits, adjusting for distance and setting as well as size.
Photos: Photograph the well head, pressure tank and septic area, any shop or barn inside and out, and the land from the house. At a foothill home or cabin, add the roof, driveway and cleared ground.
Q: We inherited Dad's place near Reedley but live out of state, can you appraise it?
A: Yes, and nobody has to fly in. A relative, neighbor or tenant can walk through with a phone and send me photos of each room, the outbuildings and the well. I value it as of the date your father died and email you the report.
Q: Can I use an appraisal to appeal my Fresno County property taxes?
A: Yes. A private appraisal is common evidence before the assessment appeals board. For a decline-in-value appeal, I value the home as of January 1, the lien date. I can't promise the board will agree, and appeals have a yearly filing window.

### Humboldt County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/humboldt-county)
County seat: Eureka. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Humboldt County stretches from Humboldt Bay and its fog-belt towns over the ridges to the Trinity River country around Willow Creek, and south through the redwoods to the Lost Coast. Each pocket has its own short list of sales, and I rarely mix them.
ZIP codes: 29 ZIP codes
Humboldt County homes range from Victorians in Eureka and Ferndale and older bungalows around Arcata to ranch houses in McKinleyville and Fortuna and off-grid places in the hills of Southern Humboldt. I hear from people after a death, during a divorce, or when heirs far away must decide about a house they can't easily visit, and they want a number this week.
- Many Eureka and Arcata houses date from the early 1900s, on raised foundations with older wiring and wood windows. I look for what's been redone and compare with homes of the same age.
- After the December 2022 earthquake near Ferndale and Rio Dell, I ask about foundation work. Bolting, new posts or a rebuilt chimney all matter, and I note what was fixed and what wasn't.
- Hill parcels around Garberville, Redway and Whitethorn may run on springs, solar and long gravel roads, and some have old greenhouses. I value what a typical Southern Humboldt buyer would pay and note what I can't verify.
Photos: Photograph the foundation and crawlspace, the roof and gutters, and any place water gets in. Show the wood stove or heat pump, the view, and on hill land the water tanks, solar and road in.
Q: Can you appraise my father's house in Eureka as of the day he died?
A: Yes. I value the house as of that past date, using Eureka sales from the months around it, and describe it as it stood then. If anything was cleaned out or fixed up after he died, tell me what changed and send older photos.
Q: Can you appraise our Humboldt house with earthquake damage before repairs are done?
A: Yes. I appraise it as it stands, damage included, from close-up photos of the foundation, chimney, cracked walls and any red tag notice. If you also need a value after repairs, I can base it on the repair bids.

### Imperial County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/imperial-county)

- Sales are thin in Holtville, Westmorland and Calipatria, so I often reach to El Centro or Brawley for comparables and adjust for the difference in town.

Q: How do I appeal the property taxes on my house in Imperial County?

Q: Can you appraise my late dad's El Centro house if I live out of state?

### Inyo County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/inyo-county)
County seat: Independence. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: September 15. Inyo County stretches from Bishop's irrigated pastures down the Owens Valley to Death Valley. I compare homes within their own town first, then along Highway 395, because a house in Lone Pine and one in Bishop answer to different local markets.
ZIP codes: 92328, 93513, 93514, 93526, 93545
Inyo County homes sit on small islands of private land along Highway 395, in Bishop, Big Pine, Independence and Lone Pine, between the Sierra and the White and Inyo Mountains. So little changes hands that I weigh every sale. Estates and divorces here can't wait for an ideal comparable, so I give you a clear value fast.
- The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power owns most of the land around these towns, so private lots are scarce. I explain how that scarcity shows up in what homes sell for.
- Independence and Big Pine see few sales, so I lean on Bishop when I must and adjust for the smaller town, fewer services and the longer drive.
- Views carry weight here: Mount Whitney and the Alabama Hills from Lone Pine, or the Sierra crest from West Bishop. Your yard photos show me what the record can't.

Q: Can you appraise a manufactured home on its own lot in Bishop?
A: Yes. I confirm it's on a permanent foundation and assessed with the land, then compare it with other manufactured homes sold in the Owens Valley. Photos of the data plate, usually inside a kitchen cabinet or closet, and the skirting help me get it right.
Q: Do we still need an appraisal if Mom's Inyo County house is going through probate?
A: In an Inyo County probate, the court's referee values the house for the inventory. Many executors still order my appraisal to decide whether to list, keep or let one heir buy out the others. With Bishop and Lone Pine sales this thin, a careful report helps everyone agree.

### Kern County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/kern-county)
County seat: Bakersfield. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Kern's markets change with the terrain: valley farm towns, west-side oil country, the Kern River canyon and Lake Isabella, the Tehachapi Mountains and the Mojave Desert beyond the pass. I keep each comparison inside the setting where the home sits.
ZIP codes: 43 ZIP codes
Kern County covers more ground than people picture: oil towns like Taft, farm towns like Delano and Wasco, mountain homes around Tehachapi, river cabins in Kernville and desert houses in Ridgecrest and Rosamond. I appraise all of it. Before anyone can keep, sell or split a place hours from Bakersfield, you need the number, and I work from your photos.
- Mineral rights here are sometimes owned apart from the house. My appraisal covers the house and land, and I note any wells, pump jacks or pipelines nearby, since buyers notice them.
- Around Tehachapi, Bear Valley Springs and Stallion Springs, I weigh lot size, horse setups, snow and wind. Gated communities carry their own dues and rules, so I compare inside them first.
- In Ridgecrest, California City and Rosamond, I separate built-up streets from scattered desert lots, check whether a home is manufactured or site-built, and note wells, septic and any earthquake repairs.
Photos: Take wide shots of the land and what's around it: a pump jack, a wind ridge, a dirt road or open desert. Then every room, the roof, the heating and cooling equipment, and any well or septic lid.
Q: Can I put up my house in Kern County for a bail property bond?
A: Many courts accept property bonds and usually want a current value from a licensed appraiser to measure the equity. I turn it around fast once your photos arrive, and the court decides whether the equity covers the bail.
Q: Mom's house in Tehachapi is going through probate, do I need my own appraisal?
A: In a California probate, the court's referee values the real estate for the inventory. Many executors still want an independent appraisal too, and I value the house as of the date of death for the step-up in basis, a sale or a buyout. Your probate attorney can say whether you need one.

### Kings County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/kings-county)
County seat: Hanford. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: September 15. Across Kings County, I separate town lots in Hanford and Lemoore from farmhouses on country roads and from Avenal and Kettleman City on the west side. Flat ground hides real differences in water, flooding and what's next door.
ZIP codes: 93202, 93204, 93212, 93230, 93239, 93245, 93266
Kings County is flat, open farm country, and I appraise homes in Hanford, Lemoore, Corcoran and Avenal and the farmhouses on country roads between them. When a parent dies or a Hanford house has to be divided, I value it from your photos.

- Country homes here often sit beside dairies, cotton or orchards. I treat a nearby dairy as part of the location, check the well and septic, and compare with other rural homesites.

Q: How fast can I get our Hanford house appraised for our divorce?

Q: Is it worth appealing my Kings County property taxes if values dropped?

- Cobb Mountain homes sit on steep, wooded lots, and many were rebuilt after 2015. I look at the slope, the access road and the cleared space, and I compare new with new.

Q: We inherited Grandpa's lakefront house on Clear Lake. How do we find its value?
