### Sierra County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/sierra-county)
County seat: Downieville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: September 15. Sierra County splits into the river canyon towns along the North Yuba and the open ranch country of Sierra Valley. I treat them as separate markets and widen into neighboring counties only when local sales can't carry the analysis.
ZIP codes: 95910, 96118, 96124, 96125
Sierra County has some of the quietest housing markets I work in: old homes and cabins along the North Yuba River in Downieville and Sierra City, and ranch houses and small-town homes in Loyalton and Sierraville out in Sierra Valley. When a parent's place needs a value for probate or a buyout, I build it carefully from the few sales there are.
- Downieville and Sierra City homes are often old, built close to the river or into the hillside, with additions over generations. I look at foundations, flood exposure, parking and winter access.
- In Sierra Valley, I check whether a house sits on a small homesite or a big ranch parcel with irrigated meadow and barns, since ranch land sells on different terms.
- Older cabins here often rely on wood heat, small septic systems and roofs that have carried decades of snow. I look closely at those, since repairs this far up the canyon cost more and take longer.
Photos: Show me the river side of the house, the foundation, the wood stove, and the roof after a winter. In Sierra Valley, photograph the barns, corrals, fencing and the view across the meadows.
Q: Do we need our own appraisal for probate on a house in Downieville?
A: In a Sierra County probate, the court's referee sets the inventory value. My separate appraisal helps the heirs decide whether to sell, keep it or buy each other out, and documents the value for basis, built from photos anyone in the family can take.
Q: How can you appraise a Sierra County house when hardly anything sells there?
A: Carefully, and in the open. I use the closest sales I can find, even older ones or a valley away, adjust them for time, river frontage, size and condition, and explain each choice in plain words.

### Siskiyou County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/siskiyou-county)
County seat: Yreka. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Siskiyou County runs from the Klamath River canyons and Marble Mountains in the west, through Scott Valley and Shasta Valley, to snow country around Mount Shasta and farmland near Tulelake. With few sales and long drives, I match homes by setting first.
ZIP codes: 21 ZIP codes
Siskiyou County homes sit under Mount Shasta and along the Oregon line: older houses in Yreka, mill-town homes in Weed, McCloud and Dunsmuir, cabins near Mount Shasta city and Lake Siskiyou, ranch homes in Scott Valley and Shasta Valley, and farm places around Tulelake. When a cabin passes to the kids or an estate needs a date-of-death value, I can work quickly from photos.
- Near Mount Shasta city and McCloud, snow load, steep roofs, wood stoves and plowed access all matter. I check the roof, heat source and driveway in your photos and note what the snow hides.
- McCloud and Weed began as lumber company towns, and many mill-era houses are small and similar. I compare them with each other first and weigh how much each has been updated.
- Scott Valley and Shasta Valley homes often sit on irrigated pasture with a well and outbuildings. I value the house and homesite against other rural sales, apart from the ranch land itself.
Photos: Photograph the view of Mount Shasta if you have one, the roof and how it sheds snow, the wood stove or furnace, and the driveway. On rural land, show the pasture, the barn and the well.
Q: Can you appraise my aunt's house in Yreka as of when she died three years ago?
A: Yes. I use Yreka and Shasta Valley sales from around the date she died, not today's market. If the Yreka house was cleared out or repaired since, tell me what changed and send any photos from before.
Q: We're giving our Siskiyou County cabin to the kids. Do we need an appraisal?
A: For a Siskiyou cabin, a gift tax return generally calls for the fair market value on the date of the gift, so your tax preparer will likely ask for an appraisal. I appraise the cabin as of that date against cabin sales around Mount Shasta, McCloud and Lake Siskiyou.

### Solano County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/solano-county)
County seat: Fairfield. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Solano County runs from the Carquinez Strait waterfront through the Fairfield and Vacaville tracts to Dixon's farmland and the Delta at Rio Vista. I keep each comparable in your town and building era.
ZIP codes: 14 ZIP codes
Solano County homes run from Victorians and wartime cottages in Vallejo and historic houses in Benicia to the 1980s-2000s two-stories that cover much of Fairfield and Vacaville, and farm-edge places around Dixon and Rio Vista. I value them after a death in the family, in divorces and before buyouts, often when someone needs a number before listing or before a hearing.
- Benicia is its own market, from the old homes near First Street to the Southampton tracts on the hill, and I don't borrow sales from Vallejo next door to value it.
- Some newer subdivisions in Fairfield, Vacaville and Dixon pay Mello-Roos or other special taxes on top of the regular bill, and I note them because buyers compare the total yearly cost.
- Around Rio Vista, river views, levee protection and flood zone maps all shape value, and I compare homes in the 55-plus Trilogy community with other Trilogy sales first.
Photos: Photograph the side yard and gate if you park an RV or boat, the back yard, and any view of the strait, the Vaca Mountains or the river. On a farm-edge parcel, add the well and outbuildings.
Q: My spouse won't let me in the house, can you still appraise it in Solano County?
A: Often, yes. I can work from exterior photos taken from the street, listing photos from the last sale, permits and county records, and I state clearly in the report what I couldn't see and what I assumed.
Q: Is it worth appealing our Suisun City property taxes now that values have dipped?
A: It depends on when you bought. Owners who bought near the last peak are the ones most likely to be assessed above market. I can value the house as of January 1 against Suisun City sales. Solano County's 2026 filing deadline is November 30, and the county makes the decision.

### Sonoma County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/sonoma-county)
County seat: Santa Rosa. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Sonoma County runs from Petaluma to Cloverdale and from the Sonoma Valley to Bodega Bay and The Sea Ranch. A Windsor tract, a Sebastopol farmhouse and a Jenner cliffside home need very different comparables, and I keep them apart.
ZIP codes: 32 ZIP codes
Sonoma County homes range from Santa Rosa tracts and Petaluma Victorians to Russian River cabins, west county farmhouses among old orchards and vineyards, and ranches in the hills around Sonoma and Kenwood. I value them after a death in the family, in divorces and for trusts, and since the fires, some owners also need a value tied to a specific past date.
- In Coffey Park and Fountaingrove, many homes were rebuilt after the 2017 Tubbs Fire, so I compare a rebuild with other rebuilds rather than with the older homes around it.
- Along the Russian River around Guerneville and Monte Rio, I check flood history, whether the house has been raised, and year-round access on steep, narrow lanes.
- Out in west county and the valleys, wells, septic, outbuildings and fenced or planted land all count, and I compare acreage with acreage, not with Santa Rosa lots.
Photos: Photograph the cleared space around the house, the roof and vents, the well and septic area, and any barn or studio. Near the river, show the foundation height and the stairs up to the main floor.
Q: Our Sonoma County house burned, can you value it as of the day before the fire?
A: Yes. I can value a home as of a past date using Sonoma County sales from before the fire, plus records, permits and any photos of the house as it was. Owners use that value with their insurance or tax advisors, who decide how it applies.
Q: I live back east, how do I get Dad's place near Sebastopol appraised?
A: You don't need to fly out. Anyone you trust locally can walk the property with a phone. On a rural place, ask them to include the well, the outbuildings and the road in. I take it from there with county records and west county sales.

### Stanislaus County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/stanislaus-county)
County seat: Modesto. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Stanislaus County runs from the Diablo Range and I-5 on the west, across orchard country along Highway 99, to the Sierra foothills near Knights Ferry and La Grange. I compare town homes with town homes and country places with country places.
ZIP codes: 22 ZIP codes
Stanislaus County is orchards and dairies, with towns along Highway 99 and the rivers: Turlock, Ceres, Riverbank, Oakdale, Hughson and Waterford, plus Patterson and Newman on the west side. I appraise farmhouses, small-town bungalows and newer tracts. When an orchard home or a Turlock tract house has to be valued after a death or a divorce, I can do it from your photos.
- Around Oakdale and Knights Ferry, I see ranch homes on acreage, horse setups and frontage on the Stanislaus River. I weigh usable land, barns, arenas and wells, and compare with other country sales.
- Patterson's newer tracts near I-5 and the hillside homes at Diablo Grande each sell in their own world. I compare inside the same community, and at Diablo Grande I factor in dues, slope and views.
- Farmhouses in the almond and walnut orchards near Hughson and Denair often have shops, wells and added rooms. I check what counts as permitted living space and compare with similar rural homesites.
Photos: Photograph any barn, shop or arena inside and out, the well and pumps, and the land from the back of the house. For a tract home, the kitchen, backyard and solar panels matter most.
Q: Can we sell Mom's Turlock house as is, and what would it be worth?
A: You can, and plenty of estate houses sell that way. I value the house in its current condition, worn carpet, old roof and all, against other dated and as-is sales nearby. That gives you a realistic number to price from or divide.
Q: Can a Stanislaus County home appraisal be used for an I-864 sponsor form?
A: Yes. When a sponsor lists a home as an asset on the I-864, an appraisal is a common way to show its value, alongside proof of what's still owed on it. I value the house as of now from your photos and records. Your immigration attorney decides how to present it.

### Sutter County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/sutter-county)
County seat: Yuba City. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Sutter County is flat farm country between the Feather and Sacramento rivers, broken only by the Sutter Buttes. Values here shift with flood zone, town and parcel size more than with terrain, so I weigh those first.
ZIP codes: 95659, 95668, 95674, 95953, 95957, 95982, 95991, 95993
Sutter County homes sit on flat orchard country under the Sutter Buttes, from Yuba City's ranch-style streets and newer subdivisions to farmhouses outside Live Oak, Sutter and Meridian. I'm usually called when a divorce needs a fair number for the house, or when a parent's farmhouse passes to the next generation and decisions are piling up quickly.
- In Yuba City, I separate the older ranch homes near downtown from newer subdivisions toward the edges of town, and I note pools, solar and updates, which vary widely from street to street.
- Levees along the Feather River and the Sutter Bypass shape flood zones here. I check the flood map for your parcel and note raised foundations or past water damage in your photos.
- In Live Oak, Sutter and Meridian, homes are older and sales are fewer. I compare them with other small-town sales in the county first, and only then with Yuba City.
Photos: Show me the kitchen and baths, the backyard and pool, the roof and any solar panels, and the HVAC unit. On a farm parcel, add the shop, barns, well and the orchard edge by the house.
Q: We're separating. Can you value our Yuba City house as of the date we split?
A: Yes. I can appraise the house as of your date of separation, as of today, or both, as your attorneys or mediator request, using Yuba City sales from around each date. One report for both of you keeps the numbers neutral.
Q: Can you appraise a Sutter County farmhouse surrounded by a prune orchard?
A: Usually, yes. I appraise the house with a reasonable homesite, using rural sales around Live Oak, Sutter and Meridian. Valuing the whole orchard with its trees and water is farm work, and I'll tell you so up front and point you to an agricultural appraiser.

### Tehama County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/tehama-county)
County seat: Red Bluff. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Tehama County runs from the oak and grass foothills of the Coast Range, across the Sacramento River and the orchards around Red Bluff and Corning, up the volcanic slopes toward Lassen Peak. I compare homes within the same band of the county.
ZIP codes: 96021, 96022, 96029, 96035, 96055, 96059, 96061, 96075, 96080
Tehama County homes spread from Red Bluff and Corning out into walnut, prune and olive orchards, foothill cattle country, and higher ground toward Manton and Mineral. Red Bluff has Victorian homes and older bungalows near downtown, plus ranch homes and newer subdivisions at the edges. I get calls when a Tehama County house goes through probate or a tax appeal deadline is near.
- Older homes near downtown Red Bluff date back to the late 1800s and early 1900s. I look closely at foundations, wiring and how well updates fit a house that old.
- Around Corning and Los Molinos, a house often sits on a few acres of walnuts, prunes or olives. I value the home with other rural sales and say when the orchard is the bigger story.
- Lake California near Cottonwood is a planned community built around its own lake, and its homes trade apart from Red Bluff. I compare inside it first and ask about any association dues.
Photos: Photograph the orchard or pasture from the house, the well and pump, the shop and barn, and the AC unit. In older Red Bluff homes, show the trim, floors, electrical panel and foundation.
Q: Can I appeal my property tax assessment in Tehama County, and what's the deadline?
A: Tehama County's deadline to file a 2026 appeal is November 30. If your Red Bluff or Corning home was worth less on January 1 than the county's value, an appraisal as of that date can support it. I use Tehama County sales from then and can't promise a result.
Q: How do we price Dad's Red Bluff house to sell during probate?
A: In a Tehama County probate, the referee values the house for the court's inventory, but a current appraisal helps the executor set a realistic list price. I compare it with recent Red Bluff sales in similar condition. Your probate attorney handles the court's rules on offers and confirmation.

### Trinity County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/trinity-county)
County seat: Weaverville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Trinity County is almost all mountains and forest, from the Trinity Alps and Trinity Lake in the north, down the river canyons along Highway 299, to Hayfork, Ruth Lake and the remote south. Trinity sales are scattered, so I compare by setting and access first.
ZIP codes: 95527, 95552, 95595, 96010, 96024, 96041, 96048, 96052, 96076, 96091
Trinity County has no incorporated cities, just small towns like Weaverville, Hayfork, Lewiston, Douglas City and Trinity Center, plus homes scattered along the Trinity River and up forest roads. Many are cabins, manufactured homes and older houses on wells or springs. Heirs who live far from Trinity County often need a value before they can decide anything, and I can work from photos someone sends.
- River frontage on the Trinity near Lewiston, Douglas City and Junction City can matter as much as the house. I note the water access, flood risk and view, and compare with other river sales.
- Many homes here run on spring water, creek pumps or shared wells, some on solar with a generator. I ask how water and power work, since that shapes what a buyer will pay.
- Near Trinity Lake and up toward Trinity Center, snow, steep drives and long winter roads affect value. I compare lake-area cabins with each other, apart from homes in Weaverville.
Photos: Photograph the water source, whether a well, spring box or tank, plus the solar panels, generator and the road in. Show the river or forest view, the wood stove, the roof, and any shop or barn.
Q: We live out of state. Can you appraise Dad's cabin in Trinity County?
A: Yes. Anyone near Weaverville or Hayfork, a neighbor, caretaker or agent, can take the photos with a phone. I'll send a list of the shots I need, pull the county record, compare the cabin with Trinity County sales, and email the report to you.
Q: How do you value a manufactured home on land near Hayfork?
A: If it sits on your own land, I appraise the home and land together and compare with other manufactured home sales around Hayfork and the county. Show me the inside, the skirting, the roof, any additions and the land around it. Additions without permits get noted.

### Tulare County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/tulare-county)
County seat: Visalia. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Tulare County climbs from the flat dairy and orchard floor through the citrus belt to foothill canyons and high Sierra cabins at places like Camp Nelson. Elevation and water supply set prices here as much as size, so I compare within each band.
ZIP codes: 25 ZIP codes
Tulare County is dairy and citrus country: Tulare, Porterville, Dinuba, Lindsay, Exeter and Woodlake on the valley floor and along the foothills, with Three Rivers and Springville in the canyons below Sequoia. I appraise farmhouses, small-town bungalows, newer tracts and foothill homes on acreage. When a farmhouse in the groves or a Porterville home has to be valued after a death or a split, I prepare it from your photos.
- Around Porterville and in rural parts of the county, wells went dry in recent droughts. I note the water source, the well depth if you know it and any hookup to a community system.
- Citrus-belt towns like Exeter, Lindsay and Strathmore have older homes near downtown and farmhouses in the groves. I compare within the same small market and widen carefully when sales are thin.
- In Three Rivers and Springville, I look at access, slope, septic, fire clearance and river or canyon views, and compare with other foothill sales rather than valley homes.
Photos: Photograph the well, pump and pressure tank, any storage tank and the land around the house. In the citrus belt, show what's next door. In Three Rivers or Springville, include the drive, slope, view and cleared ground.
Q: How do I get Grandma's house in Porterville appraised for her estate?
A: Order, pay and send me photos of each room and the outside. I value it as of the date she died, using sales from that time, and email you the report. The executor or attorney can use it for the estate, the tax basis and any sale.
Q: Does a dry or shallow well hurt home values in Tulare County?
A: Yes. A house without dependable water is worth less, sometimes much less, and buyers here remember the drought years. I note what you can tell me about the well and recent work on it, and if the water supply is uncertain, my report says so plainly.

### Tuolumne County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/tuolumne-county)
County seat: Sonora. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Tuolumne County reaches from the reservoir country around Lake Don Pedro through the gold-rush towns to snow country at Pinecrest and Strawberry. I compare Tuolumne foothill, town and mountain homes in separate groups, since each sells on different terms.
ZIP codes: 95310, 95321, 95327, 95329, 95335, 95346, 95364, 95370, 95372, 95379, 95383
In Tuolumne County I value gold-rush houses on Sonora's hills and the old streets of Jamestown and Columbia, cabins up Highway 108 in Twain Harte and Mi-Wuk Village, and homes at Pine Mountain Lake near Groveland. When a parent's place must be settled, a divorce needs a figure, or heirs want to sell, my appraisal gives everyone the same starting point.
- Up Highway 108, I check whether a cabin sits on its own lot or on Forest Service permit land around Pinecrest, where you own the cabin but not the ground. Those sell very differently.
- Twain Harte and Mi-Wuk cabins range from summer places to year-round homes. I note insulation, heat, plowed access and winter use, since that splits the market.
- Sonora and Jamestown have older homes on steep lots with stone walls, small garages and many additions. I look at how the add-ons were built and compare with other older in-town homes.
Photos: Photograph the roof and deck, the wood stove, defensible space and the driveway, especially a steep one. At Pine Mountain Lake, include the view and any path to the water; in town, the foundation and additions.
Q: Do Pine Mountain Lake HOA dues and rules affect our Groveland house's value?
A: They do. Dues, the gate, lake and golf access, and architectural rules all show up in what buyers pay inside Pine Mountain Lake. I compare your house with sales within the community first, and the HOA statement helps me note any assessments.
Q: We inherited Mom's Tuolumne County house; do we need an appraisal before selling it?
A: It's wise. A date-of-death appraisal documents the value for the step-up in basis, which can matter when you sell, and anchors your pricing. I value the house from your photos and Tuolumne sales around the date your mother passed.

### Ventura County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/ventura-county)
County seat: Ventura. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: September 15. Across Ventura County I work from the beach and harbor towns over the flat Oxnard Plain, up the Santa Clara River Valley and into the Ojai Valley, then across the Conejo and Simi Valleys toward Los Angeles County. Each pocket has its own sales.
ZIP codes: 23 ZIP codes
Ventura County homes run from beach cottages in Ventura and Oxnard to farmhouses among the citrus and avocado groves of Santa Paula, Fillmore and Ojai, and on to the tracts of Camarillo, Thousand Oaks and Simi Valley. People call me after a parent dies, during a divorce, or before a family buyout, and they usually need the number soon.
- Fire history shapes many streets here, from Thomas Fire burn areas above Ventura and Ojai to the brushy Conejo edges. I note rebuilt homes, brush clearance and insurance questions.
- In Camarillo's Leisure Village and other 55-plus communities, I stay with sales inside the same or similar age-restricted communities and note the HOA dues.
- Farm-edge homes on the Oxnard Plain and along the Santa Clara River may sit beside fields, orchards or packing houses. I note wells, outbuildings and what's next door.
Photos: Photograph the hillside or fields behind the house, the brush clearance around it, and any orchard trees, barn or well. Near the coast, show the view and any salt wear on windows and railings.
Q: When is the property tax appeal deadline in Ventura County?
A: For 2026, Ventura County's regular deadline was September 15, earlier than Orange or Santa Barbara County. After that date, ask the assessor's office what options remain. I appraise as of January 1, the date the assessor looks at for that tax year.
Q: Do I need my own appraisal if the house is going through probate?
A: In a California probate, the court's referee values the house for the inventory. Executors often order their own appraisal too, to price the house or settle a buyout between heirs. I can do that from photos, even when the house is in Ojai and you're not.

### Yolo County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/yolo-county)
County seat: Woodland. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Yolo County runs from the Sacramento River and the Yolo Bypass across flat farmland to the Capay Valley and the hills west of Winters. I keep Davis, Woodland and West Sacramento in their own markets and treat the farm towns separately.
ZIP codes: 13 ZIP codes
Yolo County homes range from older Davis bungalows and greenbelt neighborhoods to Woodland's tree-lined streets, West Sacramento's riverfront and Southport subdivisions, and farmhouses near Winters, Esparto and Clarksburg. Here I'm often asked about a parent's house passing to the kids, a divorce that needs a neutral number, or keeping the old tax base.
- In Davis, greenbelts, bike paths and closeness to campus change value block to block. Village Homes, with its shared orchards and natural drainage, sells on its own terms, so I compare it carefully.
- West Sacramento mixes older homes in Broderick and Bryte with newer Southport tracts near the river levees. I compare like with like and check each parcel's flood zone.
- Around Winters, Esparto and the Capay Valley, homes often sit on farm parcels with wells and outbuildings. I value the residence and its setting and note orchard views and road access.
Photos: Photograph the kitchen and baths, the backyard, any solar panels, and any backyard cottage or garage conversion. On a farm parcel, show the shop, well, barns and the view across the fields.
Q: Our Davis house has a rented backyard cottage. Does that raise the appraisal?
A: It often adds value if the cottage is permitted and has its own kitchen and bath. I look for Davis sales with similar second units and note separate entrances and utilities. The rent doesn't set the value, but buyers notice it.
Q: Can I keep my parents' low property taxes on their Yolo County house?
A: Possibly. Under Prop 19, a child who moves into the Yolo County house may keep all or part of the parent's tax base, depending on its market value at transfer. I can't give tax advice, but I can give you a clear value as of that date.

### Yuba County (https://www.cwift.net/areas/yuba-county)
County seat: Marysville. 2026 regular assessment-appeal deadline: November 30. Yuba County rises from the levee-protected valley floor at Marysville, Linda and Plumas Lake into foothills around Browns Valley and up to pine country near Camptonville and Bullards Bar. I give each of those settings its own comparables.
ZIP codes: 95692, 95901, 95903, 95918, 95919, 95922, 95925, 95935, 95961, 95962, 95972
Yuba County is a mix: Marysville's old houses inside the levee ring, Linda and Olivehurst ranch homes, the newer Plumas Lake subdivisions, and foothill acreage in Browns Valley, Loma Rica and Oregon House. When an estate, a divorce or a family buyout needs a value quickly, I build it from your photos and Yuba sales, not guesses.
- Marysville has many homes from the late 1800s and early 1900s. I look at foundations, wiring and how the house was updated, and compare it with other older Marysville sales.
- Plumas Lake homes from the 2000s on often carry special assessments, HOA charges or leased solar. I note each one, since they change what a buyer takes on along with the house.
- In the foothills around Browns Valley, Loma Rica and Oregon House, homes sit on acreage with wells, septic and outbuildings. I compare them with other foothill parcels and note clearing and road access.
Photos: Photograph the kitchen and baths, the yard and roof, any solar panels and the HVAC unit. In Marysville, show the foundation, porch and old additions; on foothill acreage, show the well, shop and cleared space.
Q: Does being in a flood zone lower the value of our Plumas Lake house?
A: Not necessarily, since nearby Plumas Lake homes share the same levee system. I compare your house with Plumas Lake and Olivehurst sales in similar flood zones, so the market measures the effect. Flood insurance costs and any elevation certificate also help.
Q: Can a home appraisal in Yuba County help with an I-864 affidavit of support?
A: It can. Sponsors with a Yuba County home sometimes count its equity as an asset, and immigration officials generally expect a current appraisal to support the value. I appraise your Marysville, Linda or Plumas Lake house from photos and records, and your immigration attorney decides how to present it.

### Anaheim (https://www.cwift.net/areas/anaheim)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92801, 92802, 92804, 92805, 92806, 92807, 92808, 92809
Anaheim holds several housing markets: 1950s ranch tracts across the flatlands, Colony-era bungalows downtown, older streets just outside the resort district, and view homes in Anaheim Hills. I value homes here for divorces, inherited houses and family buyouts, usually with a mediation, a closing or a court date coming up, so I work from your photos and keep each part of the city separate.
- Anaheim Hills is its own market. I weigh view, slope, pool, HOA dues and brush exposure there, and I don't mix in flatland sales.
- Across the flatland tracts I see converted garages, added bedrooms and new backyard ADUs. I check each against permits and the county's recorded size so finished space is counted the right way.
- Near the resort district and the stadium I look at traffic, event noise and fireworks, and at whether a street backs onto commercial or hotel use. A block can make a real difference.
Photos: Photograph every room, the garage or what it became, any back unit, and the yard. In Anaheim Hills, add the view from the main living area and the slope behind the house.
Q: Does a permitted ADU add value to a house in Anaheim?
A: Usually, but how much depends on sales of similar properties with and without one. I look at the permit, the size, the kitchen and bath, and whether it has its own entrance and parking. An unpermitted back unit gets described, but I treat it differently.
Q: My spouse is still living in our Anaheim house, can you appraise it?
A: Yes. The spouse living there can take the photos, or your attorneys can agree on who does. I combine them with public records, the MLS history and nearby sales, and I value the house the same way whoever pays for it.

### Antioch (https://www.cwift.net/areas/antioch)
County: Contra Costa County.
ZIP codes: 94509, 94531
Antioch runs from the old Rivertown streets along the San Joaquin River up past Highway 4 to the newer tracts off Lone Tree Way and Deer Valley Road. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and before buyouts, and with so many similar two-story stucco homes, the details in your photos often decide the number.
- North of Highway 4, many homes are older single-story houses from the 1950s through the 1970s, and I compare them with each other rather than with the newer two-stories to the south.
- In the southeast tracts off Lone Tree Way, some homes carry Mello-Roos or other special assessments, so I read the tax bill before comparing two houses that look alike.
- Rivertown and the streets near the river have older homes, some from the early 1900s, and I check the foundation, the wiring and how much has been updated, since these sell on condition more than size.
Photos: Photograph the solar panels and the lease or purchase papers, the back yard and pool if you have one, and any river view. In the newer tracts, show the upgrades inside, since the floor plans repeat.
Q: We bought in Antioch near the top, can an appraisal lower our property taxes?
A: It can support a request for a lower assessment if your home would sell for less than its assessed value as of January 1. I compare it with sales from your own tract. In Contra Costa County the 2026 filing deadline is November 30. The assessor or appeals board decides, so I can't promise a result.
Q: Does the leased solar on our Antioch house lower what it's worth?
A: It can. Owned panels usually add some value, but a lease is a contract the buyer has to take over or the seller has to pay off, and some buyers walk away. I note the lease terms, compare with nearby sales, and don't count leased panels as part of the house.

### Bakersfield (https://www.cwift.net/areas/bakersfield)
County: Kern County.
ZIP codes: 93301, 93304, 93305, 93306, 93307, 93308, 93309, 93311, 93312, 93313, 93314
Bakersfield homes run from older houses in Westchester and east Bakersfield to ranch tracts across the middle of town and newer stucco subdivisions in Rosedale, Seven Oaks and the rest of the southwest. I appraise all of them. When a parent dies, a marriage ends or relatives need to settle up, the Bakersfield house is often the biggest piece, and I can value it from your photos.
- Bakersfield summers are long and hot, so cooling matters. I note central air or a swamp cooler and its age, owned or leased solar, and the pool, and compare with sales that share them.
- On the bluffs along Panorama Drive, views over the Kern River and the oil field set homes apart. In Oildale and near the fields, I note pump jacks and pipelines close to the lot.
- Newer southwest neighborhoods like Seven Oaks may carry HOA dues or special district taxes, and some back onto a golf course. I compare inside the same subdivision and adjust for plan, lot and upgrades.
Photos: Photograph the backyard, pool and patio cover, the AC unit or swamp cooler, any solar panels and the view from the back fence. On the bluffs, shoot the view at standing height. Inside, every room and any converted garage.
Q: Who orders the appraisal of our Bakersfield house in a divorce, me or my ex?
A: Either of you, both together or one of the attorneys. It doesn't change my work: I'm not an advocate for either side, and the value is the same whoever pays. If you share the order, both of you can send photos.
Q: Can I get a Bakersfield house appraised before I make an offer on it?
A: Yes, if you have interior photos from the listing or a showing. I value it from those, the records and recent nearby sales, so you know where the asking price stands. It's for your own decision, not for financing the purchase.

### Berkeley (https://www.cwift.net/areas/berkeley)
County: Alameda County.
ZIP codes: 94702, 94703, 94704, 94705, 94707, 94708, 94709, 94710
Berkeley homes run from brown-shingle houses and Craftsman bungalows in North Berkeley and the Elmwood to West Berkeley cottages and hillside homes above the campus with long views of the Golden Gate. I value them after a parent dies, in divorces and for trust sales, often when heirs need a number before deciding whether to keep a house that's been in the family for decades.
- In the hills, I look at the path or stairs from the street, the view, the fire-zone status and the slope under the house, and I compare with hill sales, not flatland bungalows.
- Many older Berkeley houses were divided into units or gained a back cottage over the years, so I check the legal unit count and whether a tenant is in place, since both change the buyer pool.
- Brown shingles, original built-ins, leaded windows and old-growth redwood paneling carry weight here, so I note what's original and what has been replaced.
Photos: Photograph the built-ins, woodwork and original windows, the basement and foundation, and the back cottage or unit if there is one. In the hills, add the view, the stairs from the street and the cleared brush.
Q: Does a backyard ADU add value to a Berkeley house when we sell?
A: Usually, if it's permitted and well built, though buyers rarely pay back the full cost to build it. I look for Berkeley sales with similar units and weigh the rental use buyers are paying for. An unpermitted unit gets described, but I treat it with caution.
Q: How do you value an inherited Berkeley house that hasn't been updated since the 1960s?
A: As it stands, against other dated houses that sold nearby, adjusting for the work a buyer would face: wiring, foundation, kitchen and baths. Unremodeled houses near the Elmwood or Solano Avenue often still draw interest, and I show that with real sales rather than guesswork.

### Burbank (https://www.cwift.net/areas/burbank)

Burbank homes are mostly 1920s to 1950s houses on flat, tree-lined streets, with hillside homes climbing the Verdugo foothills above Glenoaks and horse properties in the Rancho near Griffith Park. A: It's not always required, but it helps. Under Prop 19, a child who moves into a parent's home can keep all or part of the parent's assessed value, depending on the home's market value on the transfer date. My appraisal as of that date supports you if the assessor's figure looks high.

Plenty of its ranch houses haven't sold in decades, so I'm often valuing a parent's place for a trust, an estate or a sibling buyout, working from your photos, the records and nearby sales.
- In Bay Park and Bay Ho, I check whether you really see Mission Bay from the main rooms or only from the yard, since that difference shows up clearly in sales.
- Many Clairemont ranch houses have added second stories, enclosed patios or converted garages, so I check which additions show up in the county record and which don't before I value them.
- A canyon-rim lot along Tecolote Canyon can mean privacy and a view, or a steep, unusable slope, and I study the lot lines and your backyard photos to tell which.
Photos: Photograph the view toward Mission Bay if you have one, the backyard and slope if you're on a canyon, and every addition: the second story, the enclosed patio, the garage conversion. Include the original kitchen and baths if they're still there.
Q: How do I find out what my parents' house in Clairemont Mesa is worth?
A: Send me photos of every room, the yard and any additions, plus the address. I compare it with recent Clairemont sales of ranch houses in similar condition, and value it as of today or the date of death. Your CPA can use that date-of-death value for the step-up in basis, which matters on a house held this long.
Q: How much does the ADU we added behind our Clairemont house add to its value?
A: It depends on what buyers pay, and since Clairemont has more backyard units than it used to, I can often find sales of ranch houses with a permitted ADU and compare them with similar houses without one. The gap between those Clairemont sales, not the construction cost, is what I credit.

### Clovis (https://www.cwift.net/areas/clovis)
County: Fresno County.
ZIP codes: 93611, 93612, 93619
Clovis runs from Old Town's older blocks and 1950s ranch homes to 1980s and '90s stucco tracts and newer master-planned neighborhoods like Harlan Ranch and Loma Vista, with rural homes on acreage toward the foothills. I appraise across all of it. Whether it's a parent's house near Old Town or a Loma Vista home in a divorce, I value it from your photos.
- Old Town Clovis has small older homes near Pollasky Avenue and the rodeo grounds, and being able to walk to shops sets them apart from the suburbs. I compare within the older core, not with newer tracts.
- In Harlan Ranch, Loma Vista and similar areas, dues, special taxes and builder upgrades vary by phase. I check the floor plan and phase, and compare inside the same community first.
- East of town toward the foothills, many homes sit on an acre or more with wells, septic and Sierra views. I weigh usable land, outbuildings and water, and compare with other rural sales.
Photos: Photograph the backyard, pool and patio, the kitchen and every bedroom, and the view over the back fence. In a newer community, include the street and nearby park. On acreage, show the well, the land and outbuildings.
Q: Do HOA dues in Loma Vista or Harlan Ranch lower what my house is worth?
A: Not on their own. In a community with dues, buyers weigh them against the parks, pools and upkeep they pay for. It matters most when comparing with homes outside the HOA, so I compare inside the same community first and adjust only when I must look elsewhere.
Q: How fast can I get a home appraisal in Clovis for a court date?
A: I email the report within 24 hours of payment and your photos, weekends included. There's no visit to schedule, so the timing is mostly in your hands. If the court needs a value as of an earlier date, tell me when you order.

### College Area / Rolando, San Diego (https://www.cwift.net/areas/college-area-rolando)

ZIP codes: 92115
The College Area and Rolando sit on the mesas around San Diego State, east toward the La Mesa line. Most homes are 1940s and 1950s ranch houses, with hillside custom homes in Alvarado Estates and plenty of houses near campus that have been expanded into rentals. I value them from photos and records, usually when heirs or a divorcing couple need to decide quickly whether to keep or sell.
- Near campus, I check how many bedrooms are permitted against how many are in use, since added rooms and converted garages are common here and permitted space is what I count fully.
- In Alvarado Estates and along the canyon edges, I weigh the view, the slope and the custom design, and I compare with other hillside sales rather than the flat tract streets nearby.
- In Rolando, I look at original details, updates and lot size, and how close the house sits to El Cajon Boulevard or University Avenue.
Photos: Photograph every bedroom, including any added ones, and the garage inside and out so I can see if it's still a garage. If you're on a canyon or in Alvarado Estates, show the view and the slope behind the house.
Q: We're selling Dad's rental near San Diego State as is. Do we need an appraisal first?
A: It isn't required, but near San Diego State it helps. Houses near campus draw investor offers, and some come in low with a promise to close fast. I value the house in its current condition, rooms and wear included, so you can judge those offers and settle with the other heirs on solid ground.
Q: How fast can I get an appraisal on a house in the College Area?
A: For a College Area house, usually within a day of your payment and photos, any day of the week. Because I don't schedule a visit around tenants, the photos alone set the pace. If it's a rental near campus, give the tenants notice and walk through once with your phone.

### Concord (https://www.cwift.net/areas/concord)
County: Contra Costa County.

Concord spreads across the valley floor below Mount Diablo, from the older blocks around Todos Santos Plaza to postwar ranch tracts and the newer homes climbing toward Clayton. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and for trusts, and since many of these houses have stayed in one family for decades, the first step is often sorting out what changed and when.
- Concord's 1950s and 1960s tracts often have added family rooms or enclosed patios, and I check them against the county's recorded size and your photos before I count them as living area.
- Homes on the slopes toward Clayton and Lime Ridge often have Mount Diablo or valley views, and I keep them apart from flat-street sales near Clayton Road or Willow Pass Road.
- Near Todos Santos Plaza and the Concord BART station, condos and townhouses mix with small older homes, and I check HOA dues and any special assessment before I compare them.
Photos: Photograph the pool and its equipment, the patio cover and back yard, the roof and solar if you have it, and the Mount Diablo view from the yard or upstairs windows.
Q: I'm the successor trustee, what kind of appraisal do I need for Mom's Concord house?
A: Usually a value as of her date of death, which generally becomes the new tax basis and helps you divide or sell fairly. I base it on Concord sales from around that date and your photos of the house as it was. If you plan to sell soon, I can add a current value too.
Q: Does a pool add value to a house in Concord, or hurt it?
A: In Concord's hot summers, a pool in good shape usually helps, though rarely by what it cost to build. An old pool with cracked plaster or failing equipment can be a wash or a drawback. I measure it with nearby sales of homes with and without pools.

### Corona (https://www.cwift.net/areas/corona)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92878, 92879, 92880, 92881, 92882, 92883
Corona homes range from Victorian and Craftsman houses around the Grand Boulevard circle to 1970s and 1980s stucco tracts and newer planned neighborhoods climbing into South Corona below the Santa Ana Mountains. I get asked for values here when a trust has to be settled, when a Prop 19 transfer needs support, or when a divorce can't wait for a site visit.
- Many houses around the Circle date from Corona's lemon-grove era and vary a lot. I note the porch, woodwork, windows and foundation in your photos and compare with other older homes, not tract sales.
- In South Corona, around Eagle Glen and the hills near Dos Lagos, valley views and lots backing to open slopes count. I judge both from your back-yard photos and keep comparables on similar lots.
- Homes against the foothills sit in brush country, and the 91 shapes access to Orange County. I check the fire maps, freeway noise and slope before choosing sales.
Photos: For an older house near the Circle, photograph the porch, original woodwork, the electrical panel and any crawlspace access. For a South Corona home, show the view, the slope beyond the fence and the solar panels.
Q: Does Prop 19 mean I need an appraisal of mom's Corona house?
A: It often helps. Under Prop 19, how much of a parent's low tax base carries over to a child depends partly on the home's market value at the transfer. I can document that value as of the transfer date; whether the exclusion applies is for your tax adviser or the assessor.
Q: Can you value our Corona house as of the day dad passed last year?
A: Yes. A retrospective appraisal uses sales from around that date, not today's. If the house has changed since, like a kitchen redone after he died, tell me what it was like then and I'll value it as it stood that day.

### Downey (https://www.cwift.net/areas/downey)

Downey is mostly postwar ranch houses on wide, tree-lined streets between the Rio Hondo and the San Gabriel River, many of them added onto, given pools or rebuilt over the decades. Q: Do I need my own appraisal if Mom's Downey house is going through probate?
A: In a California probate, a probate referee assigned by the court values the house for the inventory. Many executors still order their own appraisal to set a listing price, settle a buyout between heirs or support the step-up in basis. I value the Downey house as of the date of death unless your attorney asks for another.
Q: Will needed repairs, like a new roof, lower the appraised value of Dad's house?

### Encinitas (https://www.cwift.net/areas/encinitas)

I handle the rest from here, Escondido records and sales included, and email the report to everyone who needs it.
Q: Can you appraise an Escondido house as of the date our mother died?
A: Yes. I pull Escondido sales from the months around her death and value the house as it stood then. If you've since cleared the grove or redone the kitchen, send older photos too, and your CPA or attorney can take that date-of-death value from there.

### Fairfax / Miracle Mile, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/fairfax-miracle-mile)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90036, 90048
Fairfax and the Miracle Mile are streets of 1920s and 1930s Spanish revival duplexes and houses, with condos tucked in between and Wilshire's museums a short walk away. I appraise homes here after a parent dies, when heirs inherit a duplex with a tenant upstairs, or when an owner wants to know where they stand before selling, and these jobs rarely wait.
- Many streets here are lined with Spanish revival duplexes, one unit up and one down. I value them as two-unit properties and ask about rents, since units built before 1978 usually fall under the city's rent stabilization rules.
- In Carthay Circle, a historic overlay zone limits exterior changes, and buyers pay for intact tile, arched windows and original wood floors. I note what survives in your photos and what has been redone.
- Homes near Fairfax, La Brea, Wilshire or the traffic around the Grove trade differently from quiet interior blocks. I match them with similar sales and note whether you park in a garage or on the street.
Photos: Photograph every room in both units of a duplex, plus the separate entrances, the garage and the shared yard. Get the original tile, arched doorways, wood floors and any updated kitchen, and show the street in front.
Q: We inherited Mom's duplex near the Miracle Mile, how is a duplex appraised?
A: I compare it with recent sales of other Miracle Mile duplexes, and I look at the rents both units bring in. A unit with a long-term tenant paying a low rent affects what buyers will pay, so send me the leases along with photos of both units.
Q: How fast can I get an appraisal for a house in Fairfax?
A: Once you've paid and sent photos, I email the finished appraisal within 24 hours, any day of the week. The photos usually take the longest, and for a Fairfax duplex I need both units, so give the tenant notice early.

### Fairfield (https://www.cwift.net/areas/fairfield)
County: Solano County.
ZIP codes: 94533, 94534
Fairfield runs from the older streets around downtown and Texas Street out to the newer subdivisions of Cordelia, Green Valley and Rancho Solano, with Travis Air Force Base just to the east. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and before buyouts, and often on a deadline because someone has to relocate or a court date is set.
- Green Valley and Rancho Solano homes often sit on slopes with views and larger lots, and some have HOA fees, so I compare them with each other rather than with flat tracts across town.
- In the older neighborhoods near downtown and Texas Street, homes from the 1940s to 1960s vary block by block, and I lean on your photos of updates, foundation and roof to place them.
- Out in Suisun Valley and upper Green Valley, I see small vineyards, horse property and homes on wells, and I compare them with other rural parcels, not with tract homes.

Q: We have to move out of Fairfield next month, how fast can you appraise our house?
A: Fast, because I don't need to schedule a visit. Send photos of every room and the outside once the movers are done, when floors and walls are easy to see, and I write the report from those, county records and recent Fairfield sales. If you've already left, a neighbor or your agent can take them.
Q: Can I use the equity in my Fairfield home for an I-864 affidavit of support?
A: Many sponsors do list home equity as an asset, and the immigration rules generally expect proof of the home's current value, which an appraisal provides. I value the house as of today using Fairfield sales; your immigration attorney decides how the equity figure fits your case.

### Florin / Parkway, Sacramento (https://www.cwift.net/areas/florin-parkway)
County: Sacramento County.

Florin and Parkway in south Sacramento are mostly single-story homes from the 1950s through the 1970s, on streets off Florin Road, Stockton Boulevard and Mack Road, with some older houses on deep lots. Calls from here often come when a parent's house goes to several heirs or a couple splitting up needs a number fast, and I work from the photos you take.
- Garage conversions, added bedrooms and patio enclosures are common here. I check what the record shows against what your photos show, and I value unpermitted space the way local sales actually treat it.
- Deep lots in the Florin area sometimes hold a second dwelling, RV parking, a shop or an old mobile home. I describe each one and decide what adds value and what doesn't.
- Homes along Morrison Creek and Florin Creek sit near flood channels whose maps changed after levee and basin work. I check the current flood map for your parcel rather than relying on old notices.
Photos: Photograph every room, including the converted garage or back addition, the original kitchen if it's still there, the roof, the HVAC unit, and the whole backyard with any second unit, shed or RV pad.
Q: Mom left her Florin house to all of us. How do we split it fairly?
A: Start with a value everyone accepts. I appraise the Florin house as of your mother's date of death, which also documents the step-up in basis, and every heir gets the same report. From there you can sell, or one of you can buy out the others at a number nobody has to argue about.
Q: What is our Parkway house worth as is, with the old roof and original kitchen?
A: That's exactly what I appraise: the house as it stands, roof and kitchen included, compared with nearby south Sacramento homes that sold without repairs. You'll see what it's worth today before deciding whether fixing anything is worth the money and time.

### Folsom (https://www.cwift.net/areas/folsom)
County: Sacramento County.
ZIP codes: 95630
Folsom has older houses near the Sutter Street historic district, 1980s and 1990s tracts, the hillside streets of Empire Ranch and Broadstone, and new construction south of Highway 50 in Folsom Ranch. A divorce, an estate or a trust usually brings people to me, and everyone involved needs a solid value quickly, before deciding anything else.

- New homes south of Highway 50 carry Mello-Roos and HOA charges and may compete with builders selling nearby. I compare resales with resales and note what new construction is offering.
- Older homes in the historic district and the streets around it have smaller lots and more remodel variety. I compare them with each other rather than with Briggs Ranch or Empire Ranch.
Photos: Photograph the view from the back yard or deck, the kitchen and baths, the pool, the solar panels and any built-in features. If you back onto open space, a trail or the lake, show that too.
Q: Can an appraisal lower property taxes on a Folsom house we bought at the peak?
A: It may support a decline-in-value review if Folsom prices have slipped below what you paid. I appraise the house as of January 1 using Folsom sales from around that date. I can't promise the outcome; the assessor or appeals board decides, and filing deadlines matter.
Q: I live back East. Can you appraise my late father's house in Folsom?
A: Yes, without anyone flying in. A neighbor, the listing agent or a cleaning crew can take photos, and I pull Folsom sales from around your father's date of death. You get the report by email, ready for the trustee, your tax preparer or your siblings.

### Fontana (https://www.cwift.net/areas/fontana)
County: San Bernardino County.

Fontana homes run from older houses on larger lots in south Fontana to 1980s and 1990s tracts in the middle of town and newer master-planned neighborhoods in north Fontana, like Sierra Lakes and Hunter's Ridge. Warehouses and truck routes sit close to some streets now. I value Fontana homes for I-864 sponsors, estates, divorces and as-is sales, and people usually need the value fast.
- Postwar homes near downtown Fontana date from the Kaiser Steel years and often sit on larger lots than later tracts. I look at updates, additions and the extra yard, and compare with older Fontana sales.
- Sierra Lakes homes near the golf course and the newer tracts in north Fontana sell apart from central Fontana. I compare inside the same tract first and weigh golf frontage, mountain views and lot size.
- In south Fontana, some lots still have room for animals, workshops or RV parking. I compare them with other large-lot sales, because a buyer looking for space pays for it.

Q: Do I need a home appraisal for an I-864 affidavit of support in Fontana?

Q: We turned our Fontana garage into a room. Does that change the appraisal?
A: It can. In Fontana, a permitted conversion counts as living space, though losing garage parking can cut the other way. Unpermitted space I note and value separately, usually for less. Send photos of the room, where the garage door was, and the permit if you have one.

### Fremont (https://www.cwift.net/areas/fremont)
County: Alameda County.
ZIP codes: 94536, 94538, 94539, 94555
Fremont grew from five small towns, Centerville, Niles, Irvington, Mission San Jose and Warm Springs, and each still has its own feel, from Niles cottages at the mouth of the canyon to Mission San Jose homes on the slopes below Mission Peak. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and for trusts, when the people involved need a number quickly from someone who isn't on either side.
- The Hayward Fault runs right through Fremont near Central Park and Mission Boulevard, so I check fault-zone maps and look at foundations and slab cracks in your photos.
- Values shift between districts, so I keep sales inside the same one and match the era: 1950s ranches in Centerville and Irvington, newer two-stories in Ardenwood and the Mission San Jose hills.
- Around the Warm Springs BART station, newer townhouses and condos come with HOA dues and shared amenities, and I compare them with units in similar recent complexes rather than older condos.
Photos: Photograph the kitchen and baths, the back yard, and any view toward Mission Peak or the bay. For a newer townhouse near Warm Springs, add the attached garage, the balcony and the shared spaces.
Q: Can you appraise our Fremont house for a divorce as of our separation date?

Q: We're selling our Fremont house to our daughter below market, do we need an appraisal?
A: It's wise to have one. When family sells to family below market, the gap between the price and fair market value may count as a gift, and your CPA will want a supportable value to report it. I value the house as of the sale date using comparable Fremont sales.

### Fresno (https://www.cwift.net/areas/fresno)
County: Fresno County.
ZIP codes: 19 ZIP codes
Fresno is a big, flat city with many eras of housing: 1920s bungalows and Spanish revival homes in the Tower District and along Huntington Boulevard, big-lot ranch homes under old trees in Fig Garden and Sunnyside, and stucco tracts and gated neighborhoods across north Fresno. Whether it's a Tower District bungalow in an estate or a north Fresno tract house in a divorce, I value it from your photos.
- In Old Fig Garden, lots are big, trees are huge and Van Ness Boulevard turns into Christmas Tree Lane each December. I treat lot size, tree cover and the street itself as part of the value.
- Tower District and Huntington Boulevard homes often keep original details after decades of updates, some good and some not. I judge the quality of the work from your photos and compare with older homes nearby.
- On the San Joaquin River bluffs near Woodward Park, views and slope set some homes apart from ordinary tracts. I check what you see from the back and compare with other bluff lots.
Photos: Show the backyard, pool and shade structures, the AC unit and any solar, then each room. In the Tower District or Fig Garden, add original details and the detached garage. On the north side bluffs, the view from the back.
Q: What is my late father's Fresno house worth for the step-up in basis?
A: Its market value on the day he died. I appraise the house as of that date with sales that closed around it. Heirs and their CPAs use that figure as the starting point when the house is sold. I don't give tax advice, but the value is documented.
Q: Does a backyard ADU add value to a house in Fresno?
A: A permitted one usually does, though rarely as much as it cost to build. I look at its size, kitchen, separate entrance and utilities, and whether nearby sales with second units show buyers paying more. Send me inside photos and the permit if you have it.

Q: Can I keep my parents' Prop 13 tax rate if I move in?
A: Possibly. Under Prop 19, a child who makes the family home their main residence can keep some or all of the parents' tax benefit, depending on the home's market value at transfer. I appraise as of that date; the assessor and your advisor handle the rest.

### Hemet (https://www.cwift.net/areas/hemet)
County: Riverside County.

- Older streets near downtown Hemet hold houses from several decades side by side, in every state of upkeep. I read condition room by room from your photos and compare with sales in similar shape.

Q: We inherited mom's Hemet house. Do we need an appraisal for the step-up in basis?

### Highland Park / Mt Washington, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/highland-park-mt-washington)
County: Los Angeles County.

Highland Park is block after block of 1900s to 1920s Craftsman bungalows along the Arroyo Seco, with Mount Washington climbing above it on narrow, winding roads. - Fully renovated bungalows sit next to houses that haven't been touched in decades. I match yours with sales in the same condition, not simply the ones on your street, and I watch for flips that skipped permits.
- On Mount Washington, roads are narrow, lots are steep and some houses are reached by stairs. I look at the grade, parking, retaining walls and the view, which can matter more than size up there.
Photos: For a Craftsman, photograph the porch, built-ins, fireplace, wood trim and original windows, plus any back cottage. On Mount Washington, show the road, the stairs or driveway, the slope, the deck supports and the view.
Q: Can I sell my parents' Highland Park bungalow as is without fixing anything?
A: Yes, and in Highland Park an untouched Craftsman often draws buyers who want to restore it themselves. My as-is appraisal compares your bungalow with other unrestored sales nearby, so you can weigh that number against what repairs would cost.
Q: We have a back cottage in Highland Park, does it count in the appraisal?
A: It does if it's legal, and some older lots here have one. I check the records to see whether the cottage is permitted as a second unit, then compare with sales that also have one. If it was never permitted, I describe it but give it less weight.

### Hillcrest / Mission Hills, San Diego (https://www.cwift.net/areas/hillcrest-mission-hills)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 92103
Hillcrest and Mission Hills sit on the mesa and hills between Balboa Park, Mission Valley and Old Town. Trusts and estates after long ownership come up often here, and I help heirs who need a number before they can act.

- Canyon and bay views vary street by street, so I check whether you see the bay, the airport, Mission Valley or the canyon from the main rooms, and how steep the lot falls away behind.
- For Hillcrest condos, I compare sales within the building first and note parking, which is tight here, along with HOA dues, the building's age and whether units sit near busy University Avenue.
Photos: In Mission Hills and Hillcrest, photograph what buyers look for: built-ins, the fireplace, wood windows, tile and floors. Then the view from the main windows, the canyon behind if there is one, and the garage, which is often small or detached.
Q: Can you appraise Grandma's Mission Hills house as of the day she died?
A: Yes. I pick Mission Hills sales close to that date, describe the house as it was, and note any Mills Act contract, since it stays with the property. If the house has changed since, family photos from back then help me see the original tile, floors and kitchen.
Q: How do you appraise a Hillcrest condo when nothing in the building has sold lately?
A: I widen the search to similar buildings nearby in Hillcrest, Mission Hills and Bankers Hill, matching age, size, parking and HOA dues, and I adjust for differences like a pool or elevator. I also look at older sales in your building to see how it compares with its neighbors.

### Hollywood, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/hollywood)

Hollywood covers condo buildings and 1920s bungalow courts in the flats and hillside homes in Beachwood Canyon, the Hollywood Dell and the hills around Lake Hollywood. - In the flats, much of what sells is condos, townhomes and small income buildings. I check the HOA, the parking, and whether rental units fall under the city's rent stabilization rules before I compare.

### Huntington Beach (https://www.cwift.net/areas/huntington-beach)
County: Orange County.
