Huntington Beach runs from Huntington Harbour and the Bolsa Chica wetlands past downtown and the pier to the Santa Ana River, with 1960s and 1970s tracts filling the miles inland. I value homes here for estates, divorces and tax appeals, and most people need the number within days, before a mediation, a hearing or a listing.
- Between Pacific Coast Highway and the 405, value tends to rise as you near the sand, so I measure each sale's distance to the beach against yours.
- The city grew up on an oil field, and some lots still have an abandoned well or fall under the city's rules for building near old wells. I check records and any well disclosure.
- In Huntington Harbour, the water frontage, dock and seawall can matter as much as the house, so I keep harbor sales apart from the rest of the city.
Photos: Photograph the view from upstairs and the back yard, the street toward the beach, and the garage with any RV gate. Near the water, show salt wear on railings, windows and garage doors.
Q: How long does an appraisal take for a house in Huntington Beach?
A: Once I have payment and your photos, I email the finished appraisal within 24 hours, seven days a week. The photos are usually the slow part, so walk every room, the yard and the street in one pass and send them together.
Q: Can an appraisal help me appeal my Huntington Beach property tax bill?
A: It can support one. If nearby values have slipped since you bought, I appraise the home as of January 1 for that tax year. Orange County's regular filing window for 2026 was set to close November 30, and I can't promise how the appeals board will rule.

### Indio (https://www.cwift.net/areas/indio)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92201, 92203
Indio, the city of date groves and festival weekends, has older single-story houses near downtown, golf communities like Indian Palms and Terra Lago, 55-plus neighborhoods such as Sun City Shadow Hills, and newer tracts, some with a casita out back. Many homes here sit empty part of the year, so when an estate or a divorce needs a value, I work from photos anyone with a key can take.
- Festival weekends at the Empire Polo Club bring rental income to plenty of Indio homes. I value the house on what similar homes sold for, not on what it rented for in April, and I say so in the report.
- In Sun City Shadow Hills, Terra Lago and Indian Palms, dues and frontage matter. I compare inside the same community first and note whether a lot faces a fairway, water or a perimeter wall.
- Older homes near downtown and Highway 111 often have added rooms or converted garages. I check the county record against your photos and flag any space that doesn't match.
Photos: Photograph the casita inside and out, the pool and its equipment, the AC units and their labels, the solar panels and the view from the back patio. In a golf community, show what the lot faces.
Q: How fast can I get an appraisal on a house in Indio?
A: I email it within 24 hours of payment and your photos, seven days a week. If nobody's at the house, your pool service or a property manager can take the pictures while I pull the records and Coachella Valley sales myself.
Q: Can you value dad's house as of the date he died last spring?
A: Yes. I build a retrospective appraisal from sales that closed around that date, so the market is the one that existed then. Desert sales slow down in summer, so for a summer date I may reach a little further back to find enough of them.

### Ingleside / Excelsior, San Francisco (https://www.cwift.net/areas/ingleside-excelsior)
County: San Francisco.
ZIP codes: 94112
The Excelsior, the Outer Mission, Ingleside and Ingleside Terraces are full of 1920s to 1950s houses over garages, many on hills that look toward McLaren Park or San Bruno Mountain. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and for buyouts between siblings, and since many of these houses haven't changed hands in decades, a solid number matters for taxes and for fairness.
- Many houses here have a room, bath or full in-law unit at garage level, often unpermitted, and I describe it from your photos, check the permit record and keep it separate from the main floor's living area.
- Ingleside Terraces, with its curving streets around the old racetrack oval and the big sundial, trades a step above the blocks around it, so I keep its sales in their own group.
- On the steeper Excelsior streets, a clear view south or toward the bay can set a house apart, and so can a back yard that drops off sharply, so I study your yard and window photos.
Photos: Photograph the garage level: the parking space, any rooms or bath behind it, and the ceiling height. Then the view from the front windows and the back yard slope.
Q: Does the in-law unit downstairs add value to our Excelsior house if it isn't permitted?
A: Some, but less than a legal unit. Buyers here know these rooms well and price in the risk of an order to remove it or the cost of legalizing it. I look for nearby sales with similar setups and say plainly in the report how I treated it.
Q: My brother wants to buy me out of our parents' house in Ingleside, what's fair?
A: A fair starting point is a market value both of you can see support for. I appraise the house as is, using Ingleside and Excelsior sales, and you each get the same report. How you split costs, credits or rent from a downstairs unit is between you and your attorney.

### Inglewood (https://www.cwift.net/areas/inglewood)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90301, 90302, 90303, 90305
Inglewood is mostly 1920s to 1950s bungalows and ranch houses on tree-lined streets, from Morningside Park to the blocks under the LAX flight path, with SoFi Stadium rising over the old Hollywood Park site. I appraise Inglewood homes for heirs who just inherited a parent's house, for Prop 19 transfers and for property tax appeals, often when a deadline is already close.
- Homes east of LAX sit under the approach paths, and the noise changes from one street to the next. I compare yours with sales that share the same exposure, and I note any sound-insulated windows and doors.
- Blocks near SoFi Stadium, the Kia Forum and Intuit Dome deal with event traffic and parking, while quieter streets a mile away don't. I keep those locations apart when I choose sales.
- Morningside Park and Fairview Heights have many 1920s through 1940s homes with original tile, hardwood and plaster. I look for those details and for later additions or garage conversions in your photos and the records.
Photos: Show the windows and doors if they were upgraded for airport noise, the roof, the garage and any converted space. In Morningside Park, photograph the original tile, fireplace and hardwood. Include the backyard and the view down your block.
Q: How do I find out what my parents' house in Inglewood is worth?
A: Order an appraisal and send me photos of the outside, every room, the kitchen, baths and yard. I compare the house with recent Inglewood sales on similar streets, adjusting for size, condition and airport noise, as of the date of death if you inherited it.
Q: Can I appeal my Inglewood property taxes if my house is worth less now?
A: The county assessor will take a second look, and the appeals board will hear a formal case, if your home's market value as of January 1 fell below its assessed value. My appraisal as of that date, built on Inglewood sales, gives you evidence to submit, though the county decides.

### Irvine (https://www.cwift.net/areas/irvine)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92602, 92603, 92604, 92606, 92612, 92614, 92617, 92618, 92620
Irvine is a city of planned villages, and the era matters: older villages like University Park and Woodbridge, Turtle Rock up in the hills, and newer ones like Portola Springs, Orchard Hills and the Great Park neighborhoods. I value homes here for divorces, estates and family buyouts on tight timelines, and HOA dues and Mello-Roos taxes matter to the number too.
- I compare inside the same village whenever I can. A 1970s Woodbridge house and a 2010s Great Park house are different products, even a short drive apart.
- In Portola Springs, Orchard Hills and the Great Park, I read the Mello-Roos line on the tax bill and both master and sub-association dues, since buyers add them to the monthly cost.
- I look at lot placement: backing onto a greenbelt or the hills versus a busy parkway, a cul-de-sac or corner, and builder upgrades versus later remodels.
Photos: Photograph the view from the back yard and upstairs windows, the greenbelt or pool you can walk to, builder upgrades like built-ins or a downstairs suite, and the tax bill page showing special taxes.
Q: How do you appraise an Irvine condo with high HOA dues and Mello-Roos?
A: I compare it with condo sales in the same village, ideally the same complex, where buyers faced the same dues and special taxes. I note any special assessment, rental limits or litigation the HOA discloses, and the unit's floor, view and parking.
Q: Our divorce mediator wants a home value, can you appraise our Irvine house?
A: Yes. I take photos from either of you, stay neutral, and value the house as of the date the mediator sets. If one of you keeps the house, an agreed number makes the buyout simpler, and I can answer questions about the report later if needed.

### Jurupa Valley (https://www.cwift.net/areas/jurupa-valley)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 91752, 92509
Jurupa Valley brings together Rubidoux, Pedley, Glen Avon, Sunnyslope and Mira Loma, with ranch houses on big lots, horse setups and newer tracts off Limonite Avenue. Plenty of lots carry a barn, a shop or a second unit, and when a parent dies or a couple separates, I sort out what all of it is worth from your photos and the county record.
- Barns, stalls, arenas, shops and RV parking can add real value on a Pedley or Glen Avon lot. I measure that against sales of other animal-keeping properties, not standard tract homes.
- Second units, converted garages and add-ons are common here, and some were never permitted. I compare the county record with your photos and value permitted and unpermitted space differently.
- Mira Loma sits near big warehouse districts along the 15, while Rubidoux looks across the Santa Ana River to Mount Rubidoux. I note what surrounds each house, from truck routes to the river trail.
Photos: Photograph every structure on the lot: barns, stalls, arenas, shops, sheds and any second unit inside and out. Show the fencing, gates and RV pad, and the well or septic area if the lot has one.
Q: Does a permitted granny flat raise the value of a house in Jurupa Valley?
A: Usually, but by how much depends on what buyers here have paid for similar setups. I look for nearby sales with permitted second units, check the permit history, and value the main house and the unit together, the way a buyer would see the property.
Q: Can one appraisal value our Pedley horse property for both sides in the divorce?
A: Yes. I work for neither spouse and give one independent value either side can use. For a horse property I need photos of the barn, stalls, arena and fencing along with the house, since here those can matter as much as the kitchen.

### Koreatown / Pico-Union, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/koreatown-pico-union)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90005, 90006, 90010, 90020
Koreatown and Pico-Union are some of the densest blocks in Los Angeles: 1920s apartment buildings along Wilshire, condos old and new, and Victorian and Craftsman houses toward Pico, many split into units long ago. I appraise condos and small properties here for divorces, estates and buyouts, and with tenants, HOAs and older buildings involved, people want answers quickly.
- Koreatown condos range from older low-rise buildings to newer towers near Wilshire. I compare within the same building when I can and read the HOA's budget and minutes for special assessments and pending repairs.
- Older wood buildings with parking tucked under the second floor fall under the city's soft-story retrofit rules. I note whether the work is done and count every assigned parking space, which matters a lot on crowded Koreatown streets.
- South toward Pico, Victorian and Craftsman houses were often split into units, and some lots have a second house in back. I sort out which units are on permits and value the property on that basis.
Photos: For a condo, show the unit's outlook, your assigned parking with its number, the storage cage, the lobby and any gym or pool. For a house in Pico-Union, show each unit, every entrance, the back house and the gas and electric meters.
Q: Does the HOA's special assessment lower my Koreatown condo's appraised value?
A: It can. Buyers look at what they'll owe on top of the price, so a large unpaid assessment or a building with thin reserves can pull value down. I read the HOA documents you send, check what similar units sold for in buildings facing similar costs, and explain how I handled it.
Q: We're divorcing and own a rental duplex near Pico, can you appraise it?
A: Yes. For a duplex with tenants, I look at the rents, the leases and sales of similar small rental properties in Pico-Union, plus the condition your photos show. I use the valuation date your attorneys or mediator choose, and the report lays out every step.

### La Mesa (https://www.cwift.net/areas/la-mesa)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 91941, 91942
La Mesa climbs from the old Village along La Mesa Boulevard up toward Mount Helix and Grossmont, with 1920s bungalows near downtown, 1950s ranch houses across the middle, and custom homes with long views on the hills. I'm usually asked for a La Mesa value after a parent dies or when an owner thinks the county's assessment is too high.
- On Mount Helix and the Grossmont slopes, I weigh the view against steep driveways, brush clearance and whether the house is on sewer or septic, and I compare with other hillside sales.
- In the older blocks around the Village, I sort original 1910s and 1920s houses from later rebuilds, and I look at foundations, wiring and any added rooms in your photos.
- A house backing onto the trolley line, I-8 or a busy road like Fletcher Parkway sells differently from one on a quiet cul-de-sac, so I match those settings when I pick sales.
Photos: Photograph the view from the deck or yard toward the valley or the ocean, the driveway if it's steep, and the brush on any slope. In older Village homes, show the original woodwork and the foundation where it shows.
Q: Should we sell or rent out the La Mesa house we inherited from Mom?
A: That's your call, but a value for the La Mesa house is the place to start. I can appraise it as of the date of death, which your CPA uses for the step-up in basis, and as of today for planning. For a ranch house that hasn't been updated, I'll show how it compares with remodeled sales nearby.
Q: Our La Mesa property tax assessment seems too high. Can your appraisal help?
A: It can, if your La Mesa home's market value on January 1 was below its assessed value, which happens most often after a recent purchase. I value the home as of January 1 using La Mesa sales from around then; you or your representative file with the county, and the assessor or appeals board decides.

### La Quinta (https://www.cwift.net/areas/la-quinta)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92253
La Quinta runs from the older homes of the Cove, tucked against the Santa Rosa Mountains, to gated golf clubs like PGA West and condos near the historic La Quinta Resort. Many are second homes, and heirs or divorcing owners often want a value in hand before the winter selling season. I appraise from photos, records and club sales, with nobody flying in.
- Clubs here differ on membership: some require one with the house, some sell it separately, some have none. I keep the membership apart from the real estate so the value reflects the home itself.
- Cove homes sit on small lots and range from original weekend houses to full rebuilds. I compare them with other Cove sales, not country-club homes, and note how much of the mountain shows from your yard.
- Fairway frontage, a lake or mountain outlook, a casita and an updated kitchen all move price inside La Quinta's clubs, so I weigh each against sales in the same club whenever there are enough.
Photos: Photograph the view from the back patio, whether it's a fairway, a lake or the Santa Rosa Mountains, plus the casita, pool and spa, the outdoor kitchen, and the kitchen and main bath, updated or not.
Q: Do HOA dues and golf membership affect what my La Quinta condo is worth?
A: They can. Buyers compare the monthly cost of owning in one club against another, and a required membership can help or hurt a sale. I compare your condo with sales in the same club first and list the dues and membership terms you send me.
Q: None of us live near the La Quinta house. Can it be appraised remotely?
A: Yes. Call the gate to put whoever takes the photos on the guest list, then have them shoot each room, the patio, the view and the pool. With those, the county record and recent club sales, I can finish without anyone traveling.

### La Sierra / Mission Grove, Riverside (https://www.cwift.net/areas/la-sierra-mission-grove)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92505, 92503, 92508
La Sierra, on Riverside's west side, and Mission Grove, on the southeast side next to Orangecrest, have very different homes: postwar ranch houses and larger lots across La Sierra, and planned 1980s and 1990s tracts in Mission Grove. I value both when a parent's house passes to a child under Prop 19 or a divorce needs a fair number, and I don't need to walk through to do it.
- From La Sierra Acres to La Sierra Hills, lot size and shape vary more than they seem from the street. I check the parcel map for depth and usable yard, plus RV access or a detached shop, before picking sales.
- Mission Grove and Orangecrest are tract neighborhoods where floor plans repeat street after street. I match your plan with recent sales of the same or similar models, then adjust for the pool, lot and upgrades.
- Location inside each area matters: a house near the 91 or busy La Sierra Avenue isn't the same as one on a quiet cul-de-sac off Mission Grove Parkway, and I treat them differently.
Photos: Photograph the full depth of the back yard, side gates and RV access, any detached garage or shop, the pool, and the kitchen and baths. In Mission Grove, include anything you've added, like a patio cover or solar.
Q: Will an appraisal help with a Prop 19 transfer of my parents' La Sierra house?
A: It can. Under Prop 19, whether you move in or rent it out changes how the county reassesses it, and either way the market value at the transfer date matters. I give you that value, backed by La Sierra sales; your tax adviser handles the rules.
Q: Do we need two appraisals of our Mission Grove house for the divorce?
A: Not always. Many couples agree on one neutral appraiser instead of dueling reports, and that's the role I take: I don't advocate for either of you. I value the house as of today or the separation date your attorneys give me.

### Laguna Woods (https://www.cwift.net/areas/laguna-woods)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92637
Laguna Woods is mostly Laguna Woods Village, the 55-plus community many still call Leisure World, where co-op and condo homes, called manors, spread over rolling ground around clubhouses and a golf course. I value manors here for trusts, estates and sales, often for heirs who live far away and need it done quickly, and I can work entirely from photos.
- I note the floor plan, single-story or upstairs, elevator access, and whether the patio looks onto the golf course, open hills or another building.
- Monthly assessments here cover a lot, and buyers compare them closely. I read the current statement and check whether the manor sits in a co-op or condo mutual before choosing sales.
- I look at upgrades like enclosed patios, new kitchens and skylights, and ask whether the mutual signed off on them, since buyers ask too.
Photos: Photograph each room, the patio or balcony, kitchen and bath upgrades, the view from the patio, and your carport or garage. Include the front door with the manor number and any paperwork on approved alterations.
Q: Is a Laguna Woods co-op appraised the same way as a condo?
A: Not quite. With a co-op you own a share and the right to live in a manor, so I compare it with other co-op sales in the Village and account for the monthly assessment. A condo owner holds a deed, and I compare those with condo sales.
Q: How do we get mom's Laguna Woods manor appraised from out of state?
A: Ask a neighbor in the Village, a friend or an agent to walk through with a phone, room by room, including the patio, the view and the carport. I add recent Village sales and the records I can pull, and I can value it as of the date she died for the trust.

### Lake Elsinore (https://www.cwift.net/areas/lake-elsinore)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92530, 92532
Lake Elsinore wraps around a natural lake at the foot of the Santa Ana Mountains, with older cottages and hillside houses above downtown and along Lakeshore Drive, Tuscany Hills and the newer Canyon Hills tracts, and Lakeland Village on the west shore. When a house here needs work, or an estate needs a number before a sale, I value it in the shape it's in, from your photos.
- Lake views move value here, but so do the distance to the water and how full the lake has been. I judge the outlook from your photos and compare with sales that share a similar one.
- Older homes on the hillside streets above downtown were built one at a time, so no two match. I lean on your photos for condition, slope, parking and stairs before choosing comparables.
- Lakeland Village and the west shore sit below steep, brushy canyons, so I check the fire and flood maps and note what's above and behind the lot in your photos.
Photos: Photograph the lake view from inside and from the yard, the slope behind the house, retaining walls, stairs and the driveway. Show water stains, cracked stucco or any repair you're putting off, since I value what's there now.
Q: My Lake Elsinore house needs a lot of work. Will that show in the appraisal?
A: Yes, it should. I rate condition from your photos, so show the problems plainly: the old roof, the soft deck facing the lake, the cracked slab. Then I compare with sales in similar shape, so the value matches the house you actually have.
Q: What is our Lakeland Village house worth as is, before any repairs?
A: An as-is appraisal answers exactly that. I value the home in its current condition against sales of similar homes, including ones that sold needing work. You can use the number to set a price, weigh cash offers or decide whether repairs pay off.

### Lake Forest (https://www.cwift.net/areas/lake-forest)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92610, 92630
Lake Forest, called El Toro before it became a city, runs from older neighborhoods and the homes around its two man-made lakes, up through the 1990s tracts of Foothill Ranch and Portola Hills, to newer streets in Baker Ranch. I value homes here for estates, divorces and as-is sales, often from phone photos and on a tight deadline.
- I match the era first. An older El Toro-era house, a 1990s Foothill Ranch two-story and a new Baker Ranch home are different markets, even inside the same city limits.
- Around the lakes, I check which association the home belongs to and whether it carries membership in the Beach and Tennis Club or the Sun and Sail Club, since buyers weigh that access and its dues.
- Homes along Whiting Ranch Wilderness Park and the upper edges of Portola Hills sit against brush. I note slope, defensible space and the canyon view, and keep those sales apart from interior streets.
Photos: Photograph the back yard and slope, the view toward Saddleback or the canyon, the brush clearance behind the fence, and the kitchen and baths. If your home comes with lake club access, show the club and the walk to it.
Q: Can you appraise our Lake Forest house as of a date last year?
A: Yes. Retrospective appraisals are routine for me. I pull sales from around that date, read the listing and permit history, and ask what the house looked like then. Older photos help, especially if you've remodeled the kitchen or replaced the roof since.
Q: Our house needs a new roof, does that hurt the appraisal?
A: It affects it, and I'd rather see it than guess. Photograph the roof from the ground and any ceiling stains inside, and send a roofer's bid if you have one. I value the house as it is, using sales of homes in similar shape around Lake Forest.

### Lancaster (https://www.cwift.net/areas/lancaster)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 93534, 93535, 93536
Lancaster is high desert: older ranch houses near the center of town, newer two-story tracts on the west side, and wide-open parcels with Joshua trees, wells and horse fences on the edges. I often appraise Lancaster homes for heirs who live somewhere else, or for owners asking whether their property tax still matches the market, and both want a fast, clear answer.
- Solar panels are on a lot of Lancaster roofs. Owned panels and leased ones are handled differently, so I ask for the paperwork and look for the panels and inverter in your photos.
- Out past the tracts, parcels are larger and some run on a well and septic system with dirt-road access. I compare those with other rural Antelope Valley sales, not with subdivision homes in town.
- Desert sun and wind are hard on stucco, roofs, paint and yards. I note the age of the roof, whether the house has central air or an evaporative cooler, and any new windows or HVAC that buyers look for.
Photos: Photograph the roof with any solar panels, the AC unit or cooler, the block walls and gates, RV parking and the pool. On acreage, show the well, fencing, corrals, outbuildings and the road in.
Q: I live back east and inherited my uncle's place in Lancaster, what do I do?
A: Start by getting the house photographed, inside and out, by a neighbor, a local agent or the cleanup crew. I'll value it as of the date of death from those photos, county records and nearby Antelope Valley sales, which gives the estate and your CPA a number to work with.
Q: Is my Lancaster property tax too high for what my house is worth now?
A: Check the assessed value on your bill against what similar Lancaster homes sold for around January 1. If the sales come in lower, the county takes review requests and formal appeals. My appraisal gives you sales-based support, not a promised outcome.

### Lincoln (https://www.cwift.net/areas/lincoln)
County: Placer County.

Most Lincoln homes I value date from the late 1990s on: Sun City Lincoln Hills, Twelve Bridges, Lincoln Crossing and the newer neighborhoods around them, with older houses near downtown and ranch land west of town. - Sun City Lincoln Hills is a 55-plus community, and lot position matters there: golf-course frontage, open-space views and what sits behind the patio. I compare within the community first.
- Newer Lincoln neighborhoods differ in lot size, solar and what the back fence faces, whether a park, a trail, Highway 65 or the Catta Verdera golf course. I check each against your photos.
- Older homes near downtown and the Gladding McBean clay plant, and rural parcels west of town, don't fit the subdivision pattern. I compare them with other in-town or acreage sales instead.

Q: Can you value Dad's Lincoln Hills home as of the day he passed last spring?

Q: How do HOA dues and Mello-Roos affect our Twelve Bridges home's value?
A: Buyers weigh the whole monthly cost, so higher dues or special taxes can hold a price back next to similar homes without them. I compare your home with Twelve Bridges and nearby sales that carry similar charges, so the effect is already built into the comparison.

### Long Beach (https://www.cwift.net/areas/long-beach)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 14 ZIP codes
Long Beach is a patchwork of neighborhoods: Craftsman and Spanish streets in Bluff Heights and California Heights, canal homes in Naples, and postwar ranch tracts in Los Altos and the Plaza. I appraise Long Beach homes for people sorting out a parent's estate, a Prop 19 transfer or a divorce, and most need the number before a court date or a closing.
- In Naples and on the Peninsula, I look at canal or bay frontage, any private dock, the seawall and flood exposure. I compare waterfront homes with each other, not with houses a few blocks inland.
- California Heights, Bluff Park and Long Beach's other historic districts hold 1920s homes where original details count. Some carry a Mills Act contract that lowers property taxes, and I need to know if yours does.
- In East Long Beach, Park Estates has larger custom homes on big lots, while most other tracts are postwar ranch houses. I compare each with its own kind and adjust for updates, pools and busy-street frontage.
Photos: On the water, photograph the dock, the seawall and the view from each room. In older neighborhoods, show the porch, original windows, built-ins and any back unit. In East Long Beach, show the pool, additions and yard.
Q: My sister and I inherited Dad's Long Beach house, does Prop 19 change our taxes?
A: It might. Under Prop 19, the old assessed value carries over only if one of you makes it your main home, and even then only up to a cap. Otherwise the county reassesses at market value. My appraisal as of the date of death backs up that value.
Q: How soon can I get a home appraisal in Long Beach for a court date?
A: I email the report within 24 hours after you pay and send the photos, weekends included. If your hearing is close, send photos first and any HOA or rental paperwork right after. Also tell me the valuation date your attorney wants, since it may not be today.

### Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/los-angeles)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 63 ZIP codes
Los Angeles is many housing markets inside one city limit: Valley ranch houses, Eastside Craftsman streets, Westside condos, hillside homes on posts above the canyons and harbor cottages in San Pedro. I appraise homes all over the city for probate and trust work, divorces and buyouts between heirs, and the call usually comes when an attorney, a court or a buyer wants a number soon.
- In the hills from the Santa Monica Mountains to Mount Washington, many houses sit on posts or caissons over the slope. I study the supports, decks and retaining walls in your photos and ask whether there's a geology report.
- Across the San Fernando Valley, most homes are postwar ranch houses where pools, additions and garage conversions make the difference. I check the recorded square footage against your photos and treat unpermitted space with care.
- The city has dozens of historic overlay zones, from Angelino Heights to Hancock Park, and rent rules for older multi-unit buildings. I check both, because they shape what a buyer can do with the property.
Photos: Show the house from the street. On a hillside, photograph the slope, the posts under the deck, the retaining walls and the view. In the Valley, show the pool and any converted garage or back unit.
Q: How does a home appraisal work for probate in Los Angeles?
A: Probate in Los Angeles can move slowly, but executors and heirs often need a date-of-death value right away to plan a sale, settle a buyout or support the step-up in basis. The referee's inventory value comes separately. I work from photos, so the house doesn't need to be cleared out first.
Q: How do you appraise a house in LA with a permitted ADU in back?
A: I look for sales of other houses with a second unit, ideally nearby, and compare each unit's size, kitchen, entrance and parking. I check the city's permit record, and if the ADU is rented, the lease helps too.

### Los Feliz / Griffith Park, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/los-feliz-griffith-park)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90027
Los Feliz sits right against Griffith Park, with 1920s Spanish revival homes and duplexes in the flats along Vermont and Hillhurst and large hillside houses climbing toward the Observatory and the Greek Theatre. I appraise Los Feliz homes for heirs, often as of a date that has already passed, and for trusts and estates that need a value before anything else can move.
- In Laughlin Park and the hills above Los Feliz Boulevard, big 1920s houses sit on terraced lots with gates, long drives and city views. Sales are few, so I explain every comparison in detail.
- On the streets that end at Griffith Park, homes back right up to brush. I look at defensible space, roof and vent condition, and the view, since buyers weigh fire exposure against the setting.
- Down in the flats, 1920s Spanish duplexes and fourplexes are common, and many have rent-stabilized tenants. I value them on their rents as well as on sales, and I note original tile, plaster and windows.
Photos: Photograph the house from the street, the gate and driveway, the terraces and the view toward the city or the Observatory. Inside, capture original tile, beamed ceilings, plaster and fireplaces. Show the brush line if your lot borders the park.
Q: Can you appraise my mother's Los Feliz home as of the day she passed last year?
A: Yes. A date-of-death appraisal looks back, using sales that closed around that date rather than today's. If the house has changed since, pictures from back then help me describe it as it was. For a Los Feliz house held for decades, that value usually sets the heirs' new tax basis.
Q: We inherited a house near Griffith Park, and one sibling wants to keep it, now what?
A: Start with one appraisal everyone trusts. I value the house as of the date of death or a current date, whichever the trust or your attorney needs, and the sibling who keeps it can buy out the others' shares from that number.

### Los Feliz / Silver Lake, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/los-feliz-silver-lake)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90027, 90026, 90039
Between Los Feliz and Silver Lake you'll find 1920s Spanish homes on the Franklin Hills slopes, mid-century modern houses around the reservoir, and flat streets of Atwater Village bungalows across the river. I appraise homes here for Prop 19 moves into a parent's house, for estates and for owners deciding what to fix before a sale, and few have weeks to wait.
- Silver Lake has houses by Neutra, Schindler and other modernists, and an architect's name can draw a different set of buyers. I research the home's history and compare it with other architect-designed sales when records support it.
- Atwater Village has 1920s and 1930s Spanish and Tudor bungalows on flat lots, with more yard than most hillside homes. I keep those sales apart from the hills, where the view and the slope set the price.
- Homes facing the Silver Lake Reservoir or looking down on it sell differently from houses a block back. I note what you see from each room and how much traffic the street gets.
Photos: Photograph the house from the street, the stairs or drive up to it, the view from each room and deck, and the slope below. For a mid-century house, show original glass walls and built-ins.
Q: I'm moving into my dad's Silver Lake house, how does Prop 19 affect the taxes?
A: If you make it your main home and file on time, Prop 19 can let you keep some or all of your father's assessed value. How much depends on the market value on the transfer date, which in Silver Lake often runs far above the old assessment. My appraisal documents that value.
Q: Our Los Feliz house has foundation cracks, will the appraisal count that against us?
A: I value the house in its actual condition, so cracks, a sagging deck or an old roof are reflected the way a buyer would weigh them. On a hillside lot, an inspection report or repair bids you send show me how serious the problem is.

### Manteca (https://www.cwift.net/areas/manteca)
County: San Joaquin County.
ZIP codes: 95336, 95337
Manteca grew from a farm town into a city of subdivisions, so much of its housing dates from the 1990s on, with older ranch homes near Yosemite Avenue downtown and the 55-plus homes of Del Webb at Woodbridge. Whether it's a Del Webb home in an estate or a newer tract house in a divorce, I can value it from your photos without waiting on an appointment.
- Del Webb at Woodbridge is an age-restricted community with its own clubhouse and dues, so I compare its homes with sales inside it before looking at any other 55-plus homes nearby.
- Newer tracts off Airport Way, Union Road and the 120 Bypass may carry special district taxes and owned or leased solar. I note both, along with the builder plan and upgrades, and compare inside the tract.
- Older homes near downtown sit on bigger lots with detached garages and rooms added over the years. I check which additions look permitted and compare with older Manteca sales, not new construction.
Photos: Photograph the kitchen, family room, every bedroom, the backyard and any solar panels. At Del Webb, include the patio and the view out back. On older lots, show the detached garage, sheds and any added room.
Q: How do you appraise a house in Del Webb Manteca for an estate?
A: With sales from inside the 55-plus community first, because the age restriction, the clubhouse and the dues make it its own market. I value it as of the date of death if the estate needs that, and photos of each room and the patio are enough to start.
Q: If I move into my parents' Manteca house, do we keep their property taxes?
A: Possibly, under Prop 19, if it becomes your primary residence and you file with the assessor in time. Even then, part of the value can be reassessed when the market value is high enough, so the value on the transfer date matters. I appraise to that date; your tax adviser applies the rules.

### Mar Vista / Del Rey, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/mar-vista-del-rey)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90066
Mar Vista and Del Rey are mostly postwar single-story houses on flat Westside lots, with the Gregory Ain modernist tract, view homes on Mar Vista Hill and plenty of new two-story rebuilds in between. I appraise homes here for divorces, estates and buyouts between heirs, and with so many houses being rebuilt, people want a clear current value fast.
- In the Mar Vista Tract, Gregory Ain's late-1940s modernist houses sit in a historic overlay zone, and intact original design is part of the value. I note original windows, layouts and landscaping, and any changes that needed review.
- On many lots here the original house has been replaced by a large modern one, so one street can hold both. I compare your home with sales of the same kind of house rather than whatever sold nearest.
- Garage conversions and new backyard units are common here. I check whether yours is permitted and how it's used, because a legal second unit and an old converted garage are valued very differently.
Photos: Photograph the house from the street, the backyard and any ADU inside and out. In the Ain tract, show the original windows, walls and garden. On Mar Vista Hill, capture the view from the main rooms.
Q: Does our permitted ADU in Mar Vista count as extra square footage?
A: No. I report the ADU apart from the main house, with its own size, kitchen and bath, and compare your property with Mar Vista sales that also have a second unit. A permitted ADU usually adds value, but the amount depends on what Westside buyers have actually paid.
Q: We're splitting up and need a value on our Del Rey house, where do we start?
A: Agree on the valuation date with your attorneys or mediator, then one of you orders the appraisal and both of you can send photos. I compare your house with recent Del Rey and Mar Vista sales of the same type, original or rebuilt, and explain each adjustment.

### Menifee (https://www.cwift.net/areas/menifee)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92584, 92585, 92586, 92587
Menifee pulls together very different housing: Sun City's 1960s and 1970s single-story homes, golf-course and lake streets in Menifee Lakes, newer planned communities like Audie Murphy Ranch, and the hillier lots of Quail Valley. When a parent's Sun City home passes to the next generation, I can value it as of the date of death without anyone making the trip.
- Sun City homes are small, single-story and often original inside. I note updates room by room from your photos, because a redone kitchen and bath set one apart from the house next door.
- In Menifee Lakes and Audie Murphy Ranch, I compare within the same community first, then weigh HOA dues, special taxes and whether a lot sits on the golf course, a lake or an interior street.
- Quail Valley's hillier lots and mix of home ages make tract-style comparisons a poor fit, so I read the parcel map and your photos closely before choosing sales.
Photos: For a Sun City home, photograph the kitchen and baths even if original, any patio room, the roof and the AC. For a newer home, show the back yard and what it faces, the solar panels and the upgrades you paid for.
Q: We inherited grandma's Sun City house in Menifee. What is it worth now?
A: I can tell you as of today, and also as of the date she died, which is the value your tax preparer will ask about. Send photos of each room, even the dated ones, and I'll compare the house with recent Sun City sales in similar condition.
Q: Is an appraisal needed if mom's Menifee house is in a trust, not probate?
A: Usually, yes. Probate uses a court-appointed referee to set values, but a trust has no referee, so the trustee typically needs a date-of-death appraisal for the heirs' tax basis and any buyout among them. I provide that from your photos and local sales.

### Mid-City / Country Club Park, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/mid-city-country-club-park)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90019, 90016
Mid-City and Country Club Park have big 1910s and 1920s Craftsman, Tudor and Mediterranean houses, along with blocks of Spanish duplexes and bungalows between Pico and Washington. I appraise homes here for heirs who often live far away, for trusts, and for owners deciding whether to sell an older house as is, and they usually need it soon.
- Country Club Park and Lafayette Square are historic overlay zones with large early houses. I note original woodwork, leaded glass and staircases, and whether the house is still one home or was split into units over the years.
- Many Mid-City houses are about a century old. I look for updated wiring, plumbing, foundation work and roofs in your photos, because buyers price a big old house by what it still needs.
- The 10 freeway runs through Mid-City, and homes beside it or facing Pico, Venice or Washington sell differently from tree-lined side streets. I pick comparable sales with the same kind of exposure.
Photos: Photograph the porch and facade, the entry hall and staircase, woodwork, leaded or stained glass, and fireplaces. Show every unit if the house was divided, plus any basement, the roof, the electrical panel and the garage.
Q: I live in Chicago and inherited Grandma's house in Mid-City, how do I get it appraised?
A: You don't have to travel. Ask a neighbor, a contractor or a local agent to walk through with a phone, photographing every room, the outside and the yard, then send the pictures to me. With those, the county records and recent sales nearby, I value the house as of the date of death.
Q: Should we restore our old Country Club Park house before selling, or sell as is?
A: That decision is yours, but an as-is appraisal shows where you stand today. I value the house in its current condition against other unrestored historic homes, and restoration in an overlay zone can take time and review. Some buyers want a Country Club Park house to restore themselves.

### Mira Mesa, San Diego (https://www.cwift.net/areas/mira-mesa)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 92126
Mira Mesa is a mesa of 1970s and 1980s tract homes, townhomes and condos between Los Peñasquitos Canyon and Miramar, close to Sorrento Valley. The houses are similar enough that small things set them apart: a remodel, a canyon lot, a converted garage. In Mira Mesa, divorces and buyouts often can't wait, and I can work from your photos and records.
- Mira Mesa's 1970s houses often still have aluminum windows, original baths or older roofs while neighbors have remodeled, so I compare yours with sales in matching condition, not just matching size.
- Lots on the edge of Los Peñasquitos or Lopez Canyon can have views and privacy, while homes nearer the air station hear more jet noise from Miramar, and I account for both when choosing sales.
- Because so many Mira Mesa houses have been rentals at some point, I check garage conversions and added bedrooms against the county record and credit permitted space fully.
Photos: Photograph the garage inside, even if it's now a bedroom, plus the kitchen, baths, windows and roof so I can see updates. If you back onto Los Peñasquitos or Lopez Canyon, show the view and the slope from the yard.
Q: Can I get a quick appraisal for divorce on our Mira Mesa house?
A: Yes. I work for neither side, and I can value your Mira Mesa house as of today or the date your attorneys pick. If one of you converted the garage or remodeled after separating, tell me, so the report reflects the right condition for that date. Either spouse can send the photos.
Q: If I send photos of our Mira Mesa house tonight, when do I get the report?
A: Usually within 24 hours of payment and photos, weekends included, and Mira Mesa is one of the easier places for speed, since tract homes here sell often and I rarely dig far for comparable sales. If something odd turns up, like an unpermitted garage conversion, I'll tell you before I finish.

### Mission District, San Francisco (https://www.cwift.net/areas/mission-district)
County: San Francisco.
ZIP codes: 94110, 94103
The Mission District mixes Victorian and Edwardian flats, single-family homes on the slopes toward Dolores Park and Bernal Heights, condo conversions, and newer buildings along Valencia and Mission Streets. I value homes here after a death in the family, in divorces and for buyouts between co-owners, often when heirs need to decide quickly what to do with a two-unit building that has a tenant in it.
- The 1906 fire stopped near 20th Street, so more Victorians survived south of it, around Liberty Hill, and I note from your photos how much original detail is left, since buyers pay for it.
- In two- and three-unit buildings, I note which flat is owner-occupied, whether a tenant is in place, and whether the units are already condos or TICs, since each one changes who can buy and how.
- Live/work lofts in the northeast Mission and condos in newer buildings trade on light, ceiling height, parking and HOA health, and I compare them with similar buildings rather than flats.
Photos: Photograph each unit you can get into, the back yard and whether it's shared, the parking and the facade detail. For a loft or condo, show the windows, ceiling height and common areas.
Q: We inherited a Mission District two-unit building with a tenant downstairs, how is it valued?
A: I value it as a building with that tenancy in place, compared with other Mission two-unit sales where one flat was occupied. A long-term tenant usually lowers what buyers pay, so I note the lease, the rent and how long the tenant has been there. Your attorney handles the tenant questions.
Q: How do you appraise a live/work loft in the Mission compared with a regular condo?
A: I start with loft sales, ideally in the same building, because buyers judge lofts on volume, light and finishes rather than bedroom count. Then I check the HOA's budget, any special assessments, and whether a loft room was walled in as a bedroom without permits.

### Mission Viejo (https://www.cwift.net/areas/mission-viejo)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92691, 92692
Mission Viejo was planned from the start, and most of its homes are 1970s and 1980s tracts on rolling hills around Lake Mission Viejo and the country club, with Saddleback behind them. I value homes here for trusts, Prop 19 transfers, divorces and sales, usually when someone needs a number before a closing or a family decision.
- I check whether the house is inside the Lake Mission Viejo association. Lake rights come with dues, and buyers pay attention to which side of that line a home sits on.
- Casta del Sol and Palmia are 55-plus communities with their own clubhouses and dues, so I keep their sales separate from the rest of the city.
- Many original 1970s houses still have their first kitchens and baths while others nearby are fully redone. I compare remodel level carefully and note slope, view and greenbelt backing.
Photos: Photograph the view toward Saddleback or the lake, the slope and back yard, and the kitchen and baths whether original or redone. If you have lake rights, a photo of the association statement helps.
Q: Will our Mission Viejo house be reassessed when it passes to us under Prop 19?
A: Possibly, in part. Unless a child makes it their main home, the transfer is generally reassessed, and even then the exclusion has a value limit. The assessor looks at market value on the transfer date, and I can appraise as of that date for your attorney or CPA.
Q: Should we get the appraisal before or after we list mom's house?
A: Before, if you can. A value from me gives siblings and the agent a shared starting point, and it records the condition before cleanup or repairs change the house. If the date of death matters for taxes, I set the appraisal to that date.

### Modesto (https://www.cwift.net/areas/modesto)
County: Stanislaus County.
ZIP codes: 95350, 95351, 95354, 95355, 95356, 95357, 95358
Modesto spreads out from its downtown grid and the Modesto Arch into postwar ranch neighborhoods, 1980s and '90s tracts in north Modesto, and newer homes out toward Salida. I appraise across the whole city. When a parent dies, a marriage ends or relatives need a buyout figure, a Modesto value is usually the first thing anyone needs, and I can start from your photos.
- Highway 99 and the railroad split the city, and the south and west sides have older, smaller homes than the north. I keep each comparison on the same side of town and in the same era.
- North Modesto tracts from the 1980s through the 2000s mix stucco two-stories and single-story plans, many with pools. I compare inside the same subdivision and adjust for upgrades, pools and solar.
- Near the Tuolumne River and Dry Creek, I check flood maps and lot slope. Along busy corridors like McHenry Avenue, I weigh traffic and commercial neighbors.
Photos: Photograph each room, the backyard and pool, the roof from the ground and the electrical panel. If the house has a converted garage or room addition, show it inside and out so I can judge the work.
Q: My mom's house in Modesto needs appraising but I live in Texas, can you help?
A: Yes, and you don't need to fly back. A neighbor or cousin can take phone photos of every room and the yard, even with you on a video call. I handle the records and the Modesto sales myself and email you the report.
Q: Can I appeal my Modesto property taxes if home prices dropped?
A: If the market value on January 1 fell below your assessed value, you can ask Stanislaus County for a reduction, and an appraisal is the usual evidence. I value the house as of that date and show the sales behind it. The decision to file, and the outcome, rest with you and the county.

### Moreno Valley (https://www.cwift.net/areas/moreno-valley)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92551, 92553, 92555, 92557
Moreno Valley came together in 1984 from Edgemont, Sunnymead and Moreno, and its homes still show it: older houses on bigger lots below the Box Springs Mountains, a sea of 1980s stucco tracts along Highway 60, and newer neighborhoods heading east. Many have added rooms, ADUs or solar, which I sort out from your photos when a death, a divorce or a sale needs a value.
- Edgemont, on the west end, has older homes on larger lots near the Box Springs Mountains. I compare them with each other and with similar older lots, not with 1980s tracts across town.
- Garage conversions and room additions are common in the older Sunnymead tracts. I compare the county record with your photos and count unpermitted space carefully, often for less than permitted living area.
- Near March Air Reserve Base and the 60 and 215 freeways, noise and traffic shape value block by block. I check the map and what's behind the back wall in your photos.
Photos: Photograph the converted garage or added room inside and out, the ADU if there is one, the solar panels and inverter, the back yard and whatever sits behind the wall. A street view both ways helps too.
Q: My house in Moreno Valley needs a new roof. Will the appraisal be lower?
A: It may be, since buyers here pay less for a worn roof. Photograph it from the ground, plus any ceiling stains inside, and I'll compare with sales of homes in similar condition rather than fresh remodels in the same tract.
Q: We built an ADU behind our Moreno Valley house. How much value does it add?
A: There's no fixed amount. It depends on what buyers here have paid for homes with a permitted second unit, so I search Moreno Valley sales for those first. Send me the final permit and photos of the unit's kitchen, bath and entry, and I'll value the house and ADU as one property.

### Mountain View (https://www.cwift.net/areas/mountain-view)
County: Santa Clara County.
ZIP codes: 94040, 94041, 94043
Mountain View homes run from Old Mountain View bungalows near Castro Street to Eichlers in Monta Loma, ranch houses around Cuesta Park, and plenty of townhouses and condos from recent decades. I value them after a parent dies, in divorces and for Prop 19 transfers, and here the townhouse complex often matters as much as the unit itself.
- In Monta Loma's Eichlers, I check the radiant floor heat, the low-slope roof, and whether a remodel changed the glass walls or open plan, since buyers here pay for the original idea done well.
- With so many townhouse and condo complexes, I compare within the same complex first, then check HOA dues, reserves, and planned work like roofs or siding before stepping outside it.
- I compare homes near Moffett Field, Highway 101 or the Caltrain tracks along Central Expressway with similar locations, since the hum of traffic or trains is priced in.
Photos: For a townhouse or condo, photograph the garage, patio, stairs and the view from your windows, plus the complex grounds. For a Monta Loma Eichler, add the glass walls, the roof and the radiant heating system.
Q: How do you value a Mountain View townhouse when the complex has a big special assessment?
A: I compare it first with sales in the same complex, checking whether each sale happened before or after the assessment was announced, and whether the seller paid it or the buyer took it on. That's usually the clearest way to show how much the assessment moved prices there.
Q: Our parents' Monta Loma Eichler is coming to us, what does Prop 19 need?
A: The assessor works from the market value on the transfer date, which for an inheritance is usually the date of death. I value the Eichler against Eichler sales from around then, and your tax advisor or the assessor uses that figure to apply the Prop 19 rules to your situation.

### Murrieta (https://www.cwift.net/areas/murrieta)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92562, 92563
Murrieta sits where the 15 and 215 come together, and its homes run from older streets near the historic downtown to 1990s and 2000s tracts along Murrieta Hot Springs Road and rural acreage up in La Cresta on the Santa Rosa Plateau. Divorces and estates here often turn on one number, and I can get it to you without a site visit.
- La Cresta lots are acreage, many with horse setups and long views. I compare them with other Santa Rosa Plateau parcels, not valley tracts, and check the parcel record for size and access.
- Homes along Murrieta Creek and in low spots near it can sit in a flood zone. I check the flood map and note it, since it can change what buyers pay and what they insure.
- West-side homes against the hills often have views and bigger lots, while tracts toward French Valley are newer. I keep comparables on the same side of town when sales allow.

Q: Does the casita or ADU on our Murrieta lot count as extra square footage?
A: Not as part of the main house. I value a detached ADU or casita on its own line, based on what buyers here pay for one, and I check whether it's permitted. A permitted unit with a kitchen usually counts for more than a bonus room.
Q: My spouse wants to keep our Murrieta house. How do we get a fair buyout number?

Newport Beach homes sit on the harbor, the islands, the bluffs and the hills: cottages and duplexes on the Balboa Peninsula and Balboa Island, bayfront homes on Lido Isle and Linda Isle, the flower streets of Corona del Mar, and gated communities in Newport Coast. - On the Peninsula, Balboa Island and the Corona del Mar flower streets, an older cottage is often valued for its lot. I study teardown and new-build sales to get the land right.

Q: Can you appraise our Newport Beach house as of when dad died in 2019?
A: Yes. I use sales from around that date, the listing and permit history, and what you can tell me about the house then, including any remodel done since. Old photos or a past listing help a lot in Newport, where houses change quickly.

North Long Beach is mostly 1940s and 1950s single-story homes on standard city lots, from the blocks around Houghton Park to the streets near DeForest Park and the river, some with added rooms or a back unit. Q: What's my late dad's house in North Long Beach worth, and how do I find out?

Q: Can I get a quick appraisal in North Long Beach before listing our house?

- On the canyon rims of University Heights, I weigh views over Mission Valley against slope and brush, and I compare with other rim homes, not the flat streets a block away.

### Northwest HB / Bolsa Chica, Huntington Beach (https://www.cwift.net/areas/northwest-hb-bolsa-chica)

Northwest HB runs from the docks and islands of Huntington Harbour to the Bolsa Chica wetlands and the mesa above them, with 1960s and 1970s tracts inland and newer homes in Brightwater. - Up on the Bolsa Chica mesa, I keep Brightwater's newer homes with each other and the older tracts with theirs. Wetland and ocean views get a careful look in your photos.
- Parts of this corner of town sit low beside the harbor and the wetlands, so I check the flood map for your address and note whether flood insurance comes into play.

Q: Our Huntington Harbour seawall needs repair, how does that affect the appraisal?

Q: My ex wants to keep our Bolsa Chica house, how do we agree on value?

### Oceanside (https://www.cwift.net/areas/oceanside)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 92054, 92056, 92057, 92058
Oceanside runs from beach cottages and condos near the pier, the harbor and South O to Fire Mountain's hillside views, then inland past Mission San Luis Rey to tracts, 55-plus communities like Ocean Hills Country Club, and the farmland of Morro Hills. Heirs and divorcing couples here usually need a number fast, and I get it to them from photos and records.
- Near the Strand, the pier and South O, I separate true ocean views from partial ones, check how close you are to the sand and the train tracks, and note any vacation-rental use.
- In Ocean Hills Country Club and other 55-plus communities, I compare with sales inside the same community first, since the age rules, HOA dues and clubhouse amenities set them apart from ordinary tracts.
- In Morro Hills, much of the land is still farmed. I check acreage, crops or groves, water source and road access, and I lean on rural sales, not the tracts below.
Photos: If you're near the beach, photograph the view from each level and the walk to the sand. For a condo by the pier or in a 55-plus community, include the HOA amenities. In Morro Hills, show the land, outbuildings and the access road.
Q: How do you appraise an Oceanside condo near the pier?
A: I start with sales in your building, then similar buildings along the Strand and Pacific Street, and I adjust for floor, ocean view, parking and HOA dues. Send the dues, any special assessment, and the rental rules, since buyers near the pier often care about short-term rental limits.
Q: Will an appraisal show what Mom's Oceanside place is worth if we sell as is?
A: It shows what Mom's Oceanside place is worth in its current condition, which is what you need to judge cash offers. I compare with sales of homes that also needed work, from dated tract houses inland to worn cottages in South O, and I list the issues I saw in your photos.

### Ontario (https://www.cwift.net/areas/ontario)
County: San Bernardino County.
ZIP codes: 91758, 91761, 91762, 91764
Ontario has Craftsman and Spanish-style houses near downtown and along Euclid Avenue, 1950s and 1960s ranch tracts across the middle of the city, and newer neighborhoods in Ontario Ranch on old dairy land to the south. Airport noise reaches some streets. I value Ontario homes for probate, Prop 19 transfers and divorce, usually on short notice.
- Near Ontario International Airport, I check the noise contours and the flight path, and I compare homes under it with similar homes under it, not with quieter streets across town.
- Ontario Ranch homes are new, often with HOA dues and special taxes on the bill. I compare them with other new homes there and ask for the tax bill, since buyers weigh those costs.
- Older homes near downtown and Euclid Avenue may have original wood floors, plaster walls and older wiring. I look at how well they've been kept and updated and compare with older Ontario homes.
Photos: Photograph the original details in an older home, like the wood floors, built-ins and porch, plus the electrical panel. In Ontario Ranch, show the upgrades, the yard and the HOA amenities. Everywhere, show what's behind the back wall.
Q: My brother is executor. Can I get my own appraisal of Mom's Ontario house?
A: You can, as long as someone can get me photos of the house. A second, independent value helps when siblings disagree or the house is about to be sold through probate. I appraise it as of the date of death or today, using Ontario sales from around that date.
Q: Does Prop 19 mean we need Dad's Ontario house appraised before we move in?
A: Prop 19 looks at the Ontario house's market value at the time of transfer, and the assessor may compare it with the old taxable value. I appraise the house as of the transfer date using Ontario sales from then. How the rules apply to Dad's house is a question for your tax advisor and the assessor.

### Orange (https://www.cwift.net/areas/orange)

ZIP codes: 92862, 92865, 92866, 92867, 92868, 92869
Orange has Old Towne, where Craftsman bungalows and Victorians fill the blocks around the Plaza, plus postwar tracts across the flats and horse properties and hillside homes out toward Orange Park Acres and Santiago Canyon. - In Old Towne, exterior changes go through historic design review, so I note original siding, windows and porches, and any work that looks unapproved, since buyers here check.
- Out in Orange Park Acres and along Santiago Canyon, I value acreage, horse facilities, trail access and brush exposure, and compare with other large-lot sales rather than tracts.
- Across the postwar flats, remodel level and freeway exposure near the Orange Crush, the 55 and the 22 matter most, so I keep sales on comparable streets.

Q: Dad's Old Towne Orange house is in probate, what do we do about value?
A: The court's referee will value it for the inventory, and many heirs also want their own appraisal to price it or settle a buyout. In Old Towne I look for sales of other historic homes, note the original features and any back unit, and use the date you need.
Q: Does a back house or garage apartment add value in Orange?
A: If it's permitted and in decent shape, it usually does, and I measure that against sales of similar properties with and without one. Some older Orange lots have a unit of uncertain history, so I check records and describe it plainly before deciding how much weight it carries.

### Otay Mesa / Nestor, San Diego (https://www.cwift.net/areas/otay-mesa-nestor)

ZIP codes: 92154
Otay Mesa and Nestor sit at the south end of San Diego, between the Otay River valley and the Tijuana River Valley. In Nestor and Otay Mesa, I'm most often valuing a house that is passing to the next generation.
- Near the Tijuana River Valley, I check flood zone maps and how close the home sits to the river, since flooding and the cross-border sewage problem come up with buyers here.
- On older Nestor and Palm City lots, I sort out garage conversions, added rooms and back units, checking permits before I give the space full credit and comparing with similar lots nearby.
- Up on Otay Mesa, I compare tract homes with resales in the same subdivision and note any Mello-Roos, HOA dues and truck traffic toward the border crossing along SR-905.
Photos: Photograph the converted garage or back unit inside and out, including its kitchen and bath, and the electric meters. Near the river valley, show the street and any low spots in the yard; on the mesa, the view from upstairs.
Q: If Mom gives me her Nestor house, can I keep her property taxes under Prop 19?
A: It may, if you make the Nestor house your main home, and the county looks at its market value on the transfer date to decide how much of her tax base carries over. I can value it as of that date using Nestor sales from that time, and your attorney or tax preparer handles the forms.
Q: How quickly can you appraise a house in Otay Mesa for a family sale?
A: Once I have your payment and photos, an Otay Mesa report usually arrives within 24 hours, any day of the week. Tract homes on the mesa are quick to compare because the same subdivision usually has recent resales. Older Nestor houses with additions take a little more digging, but rarely more time.

### Oxnard (https://www.cwift.net/areas/oxnard)

Oxnard runs from the strawberry fields of the Oxnard Plain to the water, with older neighborhoods near downtown and Heritage Square, postwar tracts and newer ones like RiverPark, and boat-dock homes along the Mandalay Bay and Channel Islands Harbor waterways. I value homes here after a death, often for heirs who live far away, and for sales where the house goes as is.

Q: My brother lives in Texas, I'm in Oregon, how do we value mom's Oxnard house?
A: Neither of you has to come. A neighbor, a property manager or the agent can take phone photos of every room, the yard and the street. I add county records, MLS history and nearby sales, and email the appraisal to both of you so you're working from the same number.
Q: Can we sell the house as is even if it needs a lot of work?
A: Yes. You don't have to fix anything first. I value it in its current condition, with photos of the problems, and compare with other as-is sales in Oxnard so you know what similar houses brought before you decide on repairs.

### Pacific Beach / Mission Beach, San Diego (https://www.cwift.net/areas/pacific-beach-mission-beach)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 92109
Pacific Beach and Mission Beach pack a lot onto a little land: older cottages, duplexes and condos in PB, bayfront homes on Crown Point, and narrow lots along Mission Beach's walk streets between the ocean and Mission Bay. I often value these homes for heirs spread across the country who must decide, from far away, whether to keep the beach place.
- Everything here sits under the 30-foot coastal height limit, so I look at what's already built against what could be, and whether an older cottage is mainly valued for its lot.
- On Mission Beach walk streets and along the boardwalk, I weigh the view, the steps to the sand or bay, parking and noise, and I value the real estate rather than any vacation-rental income.
- A block from the sand in PB or Mission Beach, salt air works on everything, so I look closely at windows, railings, stucco, rust and wood rot in your photos, since condition varies between neighbors.
Photos: Photograph the ocean or bay view from each level and the roof deck, the walk street or alley out front, and your parking. Get close-ups of any rust on railings, peeling paint or water stains, since salt air shows up there first.
Q: We inherited a Mission Beach duplex but live back east. How does this work?
A: Have a property manager, a tenant you trust, or a local agent walk through both units with a phone and send me photos, plus the view and the walk street out front. I value the duplex from there, email the report to all of you, and nobody needs to fly out to Mission Beach.
Q: Would you value our worn-out PB cottage as a teardown?
A: Only if the sales say so. In Pacific Beach some buyers fix up older cottages and others replace them, so I look at both kinds of sales and see which one your house matches. Send photos of the roof, foundation, plumbing and any salt-air damage, and I'll describe the condition plainly.

### Palm Desert (https://www.cwift.net/areas/palm-desert)

- Club homes and condos sell on dues, view and where they sit in the club. In Ironwood, Bighorn or Sun City Palm Desert, I start with sales inside the same community before reaching anywhere else.

Q: Can you appraise my late husband's Palm Desert house as of his date of death?
A: Yes. I use desert sales from around that date and ask what the house looked like then, since a remodel or new pool added later would distort the value. Many surviving spouses need this for the stepped-up basis; your CPA will tell you how it applies.

### Palm Springs (https://www.cwift.net/areas/palm-springs)
County: Riverside County.
ZIP codes: 92262, 92264
Palm Springs is a city of mid-century modern neighborhoods, from Alexander houses in Twin Palms and Racquet Club Estates to the Movie Colony and Vista Las Palmas, with condos across town and some homes on leased Agua Caliente land. - Intact mid-century details, like clerestory windows, breeze block, terrazzo and post-and-beam ceilings, matter to buyers here. I note what's original and what's been changed from your photos.
- Neighborhoods shift over short distances, from Old Las Palmas to the windier north end near the freeway. I keep comparables inside the same neighborhood or one buyers see as equal.
Photos: Photograph the roof, which is often flat here, the clerestory windows, breeze block, any terrazzo, the pool and the mountain view. For a condo on leased land, also shoot the complex's pool and grounds.
Q: Can you appraise a Palm Springs condo that sits on leased land?
A: Yes. The lease is the first thing I ask for: when it ends, whether it's been extended, and what the lease payments are. I compare your unit with sales on similar leases, ideally in the same complex, because a short lease and a long one sell very differently.
Q: Dad's mid-century house is in probate. Will the appraisal reflect its architecture?
A: It should. The probate referee sets the official inventory value, but a house by a known architect, or with its original design intact, trades in its own market here. My appraisal compares it with similar mid-century sales, giving the executor and attorney a well-supported number.

### Palmdale (https://www.cwift.net/areas/palmdale)

Palmdale is mostly 1980s to 2000s stucco tract homes spread across the high desert, from neighborhoods off Palmdale Boulevard to newer foothill communities like Rancho Vista and Anaverde on the west side. - Palmdale prices have swung hard over the years, so the date of value matters. For a tax appeal or a date-of-death appraisal, I use sales from right around that date, not today's market.

Q: Our Palmdale house is assessed higher than it would sell for, can we appeal?
A: Yes. Los Angeles County lets owners ask for a decline-in-value review or file a formal appeal when market value on January 1 is below the assessed value. An appraisal built on Palmdale sales from around that date is solid evidence, though I can't promise a reduction.
Q: Quick appraisal for a divorce in Palmdale, can you do it from photos?
A: Yes, that's how I work. Either spouse can send photos of the outside, every room, the yard and pool, and I combine them with county records and nearby sales. I use whatever date of value your attorneys or the court set, and I don't advocate for either side.

Q: Does it matter if our Palms condo building finished its soft-story retrofit?
A: It does. I check the HOA records you send to confirm the retrofit is done and paid for, or whether a special assessment is still coming. Then I compare your unit with sales from buildings in the same position, since buyers in Palms ask about seismic work before they make offers.
Q: Can you value my mom's Mar Vista condo as of the date she died in 2024?

Pasadena takes in the Craftsman bungalows of Bungalow Heaven, the big early houses along the Arroyo Seco, postwar ranch homes in Hastings Ranch and condos and townhomes near Old Pasadena. - Hastings Ranch is mostly postwar ranch homes under the mountains, and the condos near Old Pasadena and the Playhouse District are a market of their own. I keep those sales apart from the older bungalow blocks.

Q: Does Prop 19 let me keep my parents' low property tax on our Pasadena house?
A: Only if you move in and make it your primary home. Even then, if the house is worth much more than its assessment, as many Pasadena homes are, part of that difference gets added to your new assessment. My appraisal as of the transfer date pins down the market value.
Q: We all live out of state, how does the trustee get Mom's house appraised?

Pomona has a deep stock of older homes: Victorians and Craftsman houses in Lincoln Park, 1920s Spanish houses and postwar ranch tracts, plus newer hillside homes in Phillips Ranch. - Phillips Ranch and the streets near Ganesha Park sit on hills with views across the valley. I compare them with each other, not with the flat older blocks, and note the slope and any HOA.
- Older Pomona houses can hide big repair needs: foundations, galvanized plumbing, old wiring and roofs. I judge condition from your photos of the panel, the water heater and any visible cracks.

Q: Will the appraisal on my Pomona house drop because it needs a lot of work?
A: If the work is real, yes, because buyers price it in. Old Pomona houses often need foundation, plumbing or wiring work, so I pick sales of other fixers and compare yours fairly. If you send repair bids or an inspection report, I can describe the problems more precisely.
Q: What date does a probate appraisal use for a house in Pomona?

Richmond runs from Point Richmond's hillside Victorians and the waterfront condos of Marina Bay to the Richmond Annex bungalows near El Cerrito and the wartime cottages of central Richmond. Photos: Photograph the foundation and crawlspace vents, the roof, the electrical panel and the water heater, plus the view if you're up in Point Richmond or on the water at Marina Bay.
Q: Our mom's Richmond house needs a new roof and foundation work, how does that affect value?
A: I value it as it stands, against Richmond sales of houses that needed similar work, so the market's own discount shows up rather than a contractor's bid. If you already have an inspection or estimates, send them; they help me describe the condition accurately.
Q: I'm the executor and live in Texas, can you appraise Dad's house in Richmond remotely?
A: Yes. If nobody nearby has a key, a local agent with lockbox access or a hired photographer can shoot each room, the roof line and the yard. I combine those photos with county records and Richmond sales, and the report reaches you by email, ready for the attorney.

Riverside's housing goes back to the citrus boom: Victorians near downtown and the Mission Inn, Craftsman and Spanish revival bungalows in the Wood Streets, grove lots along Victoria Avenue, and postwar ranch tracts across the city. - In the Wood Streets and other older districts, I look at what's original: built-ins, wood windows, hardwood floors, porches and detached garages. Your photos tell me how much survives and how much has changed.
- Historic designation matters here. If a house is a city landmark or sits in a historic district, I note it, because it affects what an owner can change and how buyers see the house.
- Grove lots in the Arlington Heights greenbelt and larger parcels along Victoria Avenue don't compare with standard tract lots, so I search for sales with similar land and trees.

Q: One of us will move into our parents' Riverside house. Do we need an appraisal?

Q: Our old Craftsman needs foundation and electrical work. How will that affect the appraisal?
A: Buyers of old Riverside houses expect some work, but big-ticket items still lower what they'll pay. Photograph the foundation, the panel and any old wiring you can see, and send any inspection report. I compare with older homes that sold needing similar work.

Q: Should I get an appraisal before selling my house in Stanford Ranch?

Q: Our divorce mediator in Rocklin wants a home appraisal. What do we need to send?

Q: How much does a bay view add to a Russian Hill condo?

Q: Can you value our Polk Gulch condo before our court date next week?

Q: Can I use my Sacramento house for a bail property bond?
A: Often, yes. Where the Sacramento court accepts a property bond, it generally wants proof of the home's value, and a current appraisal is the usual way to show it. I appraise your house from photos and records; the court or your attorney tells you what else to file.

### Salinas (https://www.cwift.net/areas/salinas)
County: Monterey County.

Salinas sits at the head of the valley, with older homes in Oldtown and near the Steinbeck House on Central Avenue, postwar ranch neighborhoods across the middle of town and in the Alisal, and newer subdivisions like Creekbridge and Williams Ranch. - Fog and wind off Monterey Bay keep summers mild, so many older Salinas homes have no air conditioning. I look instead at heating, windows, roof condition and any moisture or wood rot in your photos.
- Homes on the edges of town can back onto farm fields, a creek or a busy road. I note what's behind the fence and compare with similar edge lots.

Q: Does our garage conversion in Salinas count as extra living space in the appraisal?
A: If it was permitted, I count it as living area. If not, I still describe it and give it whatever value local sales support, but the report says it isn't permitted. Either way, I account for losing the garage, which buyers notice. Photos of the room and any permit card help.
Q: Can one spouse order the appraisal of our house without the other?
A: Yes. I stay neutral either way, and the value doesn't depend on who orders or pays. If only one of you can get photos, that's fine; I note who supplied them. Both attorneys can share the report, which keeps the conversation on one number.

### San Diego (https://www.cwift.net/areas/san-diego)

Wherever you are in the city, I work from your photos and records for an estate, a divorce, a tax appeal or a family buyout.

- Planes leaving the airport fly right over Ocean Beach and parts of Point Loma, so I weigh the noise and compare with sales under the same flight path, not quieter streets.
