Q: What does an appraisal for probate in San Diego involve?
A: It starts with the date of death: I value the house as of that date with sales from its own community, Point Loma sales for a Point Loma house, and explain my choices so the executor, attorney and heirs can follow them. In San Diego probate cases, the referee separately values it for the court's inventory.
Q: Can an appraisal lower the property taxes on the San Diego house we bought last year?
A: If you bought recently, your San Diego assessed value is usually close to what you paid. If similar homes nearby, say in your part of Clairemont or Scripps Ranch, sold for less around January 1, an appraisal as of that date can support a decline-in-value appeal. If it doesn't, I'll tell you.

### San Jose (https://www.cwift.net/areas/san-jose)
County: Santa Clara County.
ZIP codes: 30 ZIP codes
San Jose is a big city of distinct neighborhoods, from Willow Glen and the Rose Garden to Almaden Valley, Evergreen, Berryessa, Cambrian and downtown's condo towers, most of it built on former orchard land after the war. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and before family buyouts, and in a city this size the first job is picking sales from the right neighborhood.
- Downtown condo towers trade on floor, view, parking and HOA dues, and I compare a unit with others in the same tower or its close neighbors rather than with houses.

Q: Do we each need our own appraiser for our San Jose house in the divorce?
A: Not necessarily. Plenty of divorcing spouses agree on one neutral appraiser to save time and money, and I write the report the same way whoever orders it. If you can't agree, each side can hire its own, and I'd ask that both appraisers see the same photos.
Q: Is a probate appraisal different from a regular appraisal for my mom's San Jose house?
A: The method is the same, but the date is usually her date of death, not today, and the purpose is stated for the estate. In California a probate referee also values the property for the court, and my report gives the executor an independent, documented number for basis and for any sale or buyout.

### San Mateo (https://www.cwift.net/areas/san-mateo)
County: San Mateo County.

Q: Will my San Mateo house be reassessed when my kids inherit it?
A: Under Prop 19, usually yes unless one of them moves in as a primary residence, and even then value beyond a set limit gets added. That's why the market value at the transfer, often the date of death, matters so much on a house bought decades ago. I provide that value; your tax advisor applies it.
Q: If we get an appraisal now but list in spring, is it still good?
A: An appraisal is a value as of one date, so it stays valid for that date, which is what estates and divorces often need. For pricing a spring listing, San Mateo's market can move in a few months, and I can update the value later with fresh sales.

### Santa Barbara (https://www.cwift.net/areas/santa-barbara)

Q: Does a Santa Barbara guest house count in the appraisal if it's unpermitted?
A: I describe it and include your photos of it in the report, but I don't treat it like permitted living space. Buyers here know the difference. If you have any permit history, even old, send it, because a legal unit is valued very differently.
Q: Our Riviera house has old foundation cracks, will that lower the appraisal?
A: It depends what they are. Hairline cracks in an old hillside house are common; active movement is a different story. Send clear photos and any inspection or engineer's report, and I'll value the house as it is against sales of similar older homes on the hill.

Q: Does a high HOA fee lower the value of a Santa Clarita townhome?

In Santa Monica, homes range from Craftsman and beach cottages in Ocean Park to big lots on tree-lined streets north of Montana, with postwar houses in Sunset Park and condos throughout. - Along the hillside edges, from Wood Ranch to the canyons on the north side, I weigh views and open space against brush exposure and insurance questions, and treat view lots and flat lots separately.
- Many of Simi's 1960s and 1970s single-story homes have been updated piece by piece. I compare roof, windows, kitchen, baths and pool condition carefully, since those vary a lot from house to house.
- I compare Wood Ranch and other HOA tracts inside their own associations first, noting dues and whether a lot backs onto the golf course, open space or a busy parkway.
Photos: Photograph the hillside or open space behind the house, the brush clearance, the pool and yard, and the view from the back of the house. Inside, show the kitchen, baths and any added rooms.
Q: Our Simi Valley house went up since we separated, which value counts?
A: That's for your attorneys or the court to decide, not me. I can appraise as of the separation date, as of today, or both, using sales from around each date, so everyone can see the difference clearly.
Q: Can an appraisal lower my Simi Valley property taxes if values dropped?
A: It can't by itself, but it can back up a request. I value the home as of January 1, using Simi Valley sales from around then. In 2026, Ventura County's regular filing window closed September 15, earlier than Orange or Santa Barbara County's, so check the dates early.

### South LA / Historic South Central, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/south-la-historic-south-central)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90011, 90003, 90037
South LA and Historic South Central have some of the oldest housing in Los Angeles: small 1900s to 1920s cottages and bungalows on narrow lots, some with a second house behind, plus duplexes and small apartment buildings off Central Avenue. I appraise homes here for probate, trusts and family buyouts, and the court or the heirs usually want the value soon.
- Many lots here hold two or three houses, a front bungalow with one or more behind it. I count each unit from the records and your photos, and I separate permitted units from ones added without permits.
- East toward Alameda Street and along the A Line tracks, homes share blocks with warehouses, rail and auto shops. I compare a house next to industrial use with sales in a similar setting.
- Small lots and narrow driveways mean parking is often a single-car garage at the back or none at all. I note the garage, any carport and the driveway, since off-street parking counts with buyers here.
Photos: Photograph every house on the lot, with each entrance, kitchen and bath. Show the driveway, the garage inside and out, the electrical meters and panels, the roof and the base of the house where the foundation shows.
Q: Grandma's house in South LA has a back unit, how is that appraised for probate?
A: I value the whole property as of the date of death, counting the back unit if it's permitted and noting it separately if it isn't. I compare with nearby sales of lots with two houses. The probate referee sets the court's value; mine helps with the buyout and tax basis.
Q: My mother's house near Central Avenue needs major repairs, what will it appraise for?
A: I can't say until I see the photos and the sales, but I'll value it as it stands, compared with nearby houses that sold needing similar work. If the roof, foundation or wiring is failing, show me clearly, and send any repair bids.

### South Santa Ana, Santa Ana (https://www.cwift.net/areas/south-santa-ana)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92704, 92707
South Santa Ana is mostly 1950s and 1960s single-story houses on small lots, with condos and townhomes mixed in near South Coast Metro and the Costa Mesa line, and busy corridors like Bristol Street and MacArthur Boulevard running through. I value homes here when a parent dies and the house passes to the heirs, and for buyouts, usually with a date already on the calendar.
- Houses facing Bristol Street, MacArthur Boulevard or Edinger Avenue, or backing onto commercial lots, carry traffic and noise, so I weigh them against similar locations rather than quiet interior streets.
- Near South Coast Metro, I compare condos and townhomes within their own complex first and note HOA dues, parking and whether the unit faces a courtyard or a busy street.
- Sales just over the line in Costa Mesa can look like twins on a map. I use them only when the streets and houses truly line up, and I explain the choice in the report.
Photos: Photograph each room, any converted garage or back unit, and the front of the house with the street. For a condo or townhome, include the parking, the patio and the view from the main windows.
Q: We inherited dad's house in south Santa Ana, what do we do first?
A: Take photos before anything is moved or repaired, then get a date-of-death value. That number usually sets your new tax basis and gives everyone a fair starting point if one of you wants to keep the house. I can do it from those photos and county records.
Q: Our condo HOA just announced a special assessment, does that lower the value?
A: It can, because buyers count it as a cost that comes with the unit. I note the amount owed, what it pays for and whether it's been paid, and I compare with sales in the same complex before and after it was announced. Send the HOA letter with your photos.

### Southwest Chula Vista / Otay, Chula Vista (https://www.cwift.net/areas/southwest-chula-vista-otay)

Southwest Chula Vista and the Otay area stretch west of I-805 down toward the Otay River valley. In this part of Chula Vista I'm usually called when a parent's house is passing to the children or being sold as is.

- Homes near Main Street's industrial yards, the I-5 and trolley corridor, or busy Broadway don't sell like those on quiet interior streets, so I match surroundings when I pick sales.
- Along the Otay River valley and the regional park, I check flood maps, slope and the open-space view, since backing onto open land often adds appeal.

Q: We inherited our parents' house in southwest Chula Vista. Where do we start?
A: Start with a value as of the date of death, which your CPA will want for the heirs' tax basis. Send photos of the house and anything else on the lot, since lots here often hold a second building. I compare with nearby Castle Park and Otay-area sales, not newer Eastlake homes.
Q: Will the appraisal reflect the work Mom's Castle Park house needs if we sell as is?
A: Yes. I value the house in the condition your photos show, using sales of other homes in southwest Chula Vista that sold needing work. That gives you a realistic as-is number to weigh against investor offers, and the report lists the issues I saw so the other heirs see the same picture.

### Stockton (https://www.cwift.net/areas/stockton)
County: San Joaquin County.
ZIP codes: 95202, 95203, 95204, 95205, 95206, 95207, 95209, 95210, 95212, 95215, 95219
Stockton is a port city on the Delta, and its homes range from older houses near Victory Park, the Miracle Mile and the University of the Pacific to postwar ranch homes in Lincoln Village, waterfront houses on the sloughs, and 1990s and 2000s tracts in Spanos Park, Brookside and Weston Ranch. I appraise all of them for estates, divorces and family sales, starting from your photos.
- Waterfront homes on Stockton's sloughs trade on the dock, boat access and the view. I compare them with other water sales, not with homes a block inland, and note how the house sits against the levee.
- Much of Stockton is behind levees, and flood zones can change from one neighborhood to the next. I check the map for your address and use sales from the same zone where I can.
- Older homes near Victory Park and the Miracle Mile range widely in upkeep and original detail. I judge the updates from your photos and compare with similar older homes nearby.
Photos: If you're on the water, photograph the dock, the gangway, the view across the slough and the levee side. Inland, show the yard, the roof and every room. In older homes, add original woodwork and the electrical panel.
Q: Does a private dock add value to our Stockton house on the slough?
A: Usually, when it's usable and in good repair, because buyers looking for water access pay for it. I compare with other slough-front sales that have docks and look at the dock's condition, the water access and the view in your photos.
Q: Does a Stockton condo appraisal consider the HOA dues and rules?
A: Yes. Dues, what they cover, rental limits and any special assessments all affect what buyers pay. I compare with sales in the same complex first, then similar complexes nearby. Send me the dues amount and any assessment notices along with photos of the unit and grounds.

### Sunnyvale (https://www.cwift.net/areas/sunnyvale)
County: Santa Clara County.
ZIP codes: 94085, 94086, 94087, 94089
Sunnyvale homes run from the old blocks around Murphy Avenue to Eichler neighborhoods, 1950s ranch tracts in Cherry Chase and Birdland, and townhouses and condos near the Caltrain line. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and before family buyouts, and with so many original postwar houses, condition and updates often decide the number more than size.
- With so many Eichlers in Sunnyvale, I can usually find Eichler sales to compare, and I grade each one on its atrium, glass, roof insulation and how well a remodel respected the design.
- In the older blocks near Murphy Avenue, homes range from pre-war bungalows to new two-stories on the same street, and I keep those sales apart from the tract houses farther south.
- North of Central Expressway, homes sit nearer the office parks and Moffett Field, and I compare them with other north-side sales rather than with neighborhoods south of El Camino.
Photos: For an Eichler, photograph the atrium if you have one, the glass walls, the ceiling beams and the roof. For any house, show the kitchen and baths, the back yard, and the ADU or garage conversion inside and out.
Q: We added a permitted ADU to our Sunnyvale house, how do you value it?
A: I look for Sunnyvale and nearby sales with a similar permitted unit and compare size, separate entrance, kitchen and parking. If there aren't enough, I study the rent the unit could bring and how buyers have treated it, and I explain the method plainly in the report.
Q: Mom's Sunnyvale Eichler is all original, is it worth more or less as is?
A: It depends on what original means. An untouched Eichler with sound radiant heat and a good roof can draw strong interest, while leaking floor pipes, a failing roof or old wiring pull value down. I compare it with Eichler sales in similar condition so the answer comes from the market.

### Sunset District, San Francisco (https://www.cwift.net/areas/sunset-district)
County: San Francisco.
ZIP codes: 94122, 94116
The Sunset District, from the Inner Sunset by Golden Gate Park out to Ocean Beach and south through Parkside, is mostly 1930s and 1940s stucco row houses built by Doelger and others, with living space over a garage and rooms behind it. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and before sibling buyouts, often for houses the same family has owned since they were new.
- Rows of Doelger houses look alike from the street, so I study the inside: whether the original tile baths and kitchen survive, how the rear rooms were finished, and what the permit record shows.
- Closer to Ocean Beach, salt air and wind wear on windows, paint and stucco faster, and I look for that in your photos and compare with homes the same distance from the water.
- Golden Gate Heights and the higher Parkside blocks can have ocean or city views, while the outer avenues get more fog, so I keep comparables within a few avenues of yours.
Photos: Photograph the garage level and the rooms behind it, the rear stairs and yard, the original tile bath if you still have one, and the windows on the ocean side. Add any view from the front room.
Q: If we rent out our late parents' Sunset District house, does Prop 19 still help?
A: Generally no. The Prop 19 exclusion is for a child who makes the house a primary home; if it becomes a rental, it's reassessed at market value as of the transfer. I build that value from Sunset row-house sales near the date of death. Confirm details with a tax advisor.
Q: What's an Outer Sunset house worth as is, with the original 1940s kitchen?
A: I value it as it stands against other Sunset sales with original kitchens and baths. Plenty of buyers here look for exactly that kind of house to update, so an untouched one isn't hard to compare. Your photos of the kitchen, baths and garage level matter most.

### Temecula (https://www.cwift.net/areas/temecula)

Temecula homes range from older Meadowview and Old Town streets to planned communities like Redhawk, Paloma del Sol, Wolf Creek and Harveston, and acreage among the vineyards east of town along Rancho California Road. - Redhawk, Wolf Creek and Harveston come with HOA dues and, often, Mello-Roos. I check the tax bill and compare with homes in the same community, so the yearly cost shows up in the comparison.

Q: How soon can I get an appraisal of my Temecula house for a court date?
A: Pay and send the photos, and you'll have my report within 24 hours, any day of the week. The quickest orders come with clear photos of every room, the yard and the view, plus anything the county record wouldn't show, like a finished casita.
Q: Does a Prop 19 transfer need the value from the day mom died?
A: For an inheritance, the change in ownership usually happens on the date of death, so that's the date I value. Your tax adviser or the assessor decides how Prop 19 applies; my job is a supported market value for that day, built from Temecula sales near it.

### Tenderloin / Civic Center, San Francisco (https://www.cwift.net/areas/tenderloin-civic-center)
County: San Francisco.
ZIP codes: 94102
Homes in the Tenderloin and Civic Center are mostly condos: units in converted early-1900s apartment buildings, lofts, and newer towers along Market Street and toward Hayes Valley, a few blocks from City Hall. - Most buildings here went up in the years after 1906, so I check what seismic and facade work has been done, since unfinished work can mean a special assessment for every owner.
- In the newer towers near Market Street, I compare units in the same building first, matching floor, view, parking and HOA dues, and I note any resale price restriction recorded on the unit.
- Hayes Valley's Victorians and newer condos along Octavia Boulevard trade in a different market from the blocks east of Van Ness, and I keep those sales separate.

Q: Is my Civic Center condo worth less than I paid, and how would I know?
A: It's a fair question here, where some condos have resold below their earlier prices. I compare your unit with recent sales in your building and similar buildings nearby, adjusting for floor, view, parking and HOA dues, and give you a supported value as of a specific date.
Q: Can an appraisal help me appeal the property tax on my Tenderloin condo?
A: It can support one. If the unit's market value on January 1 was below its assessed value, you can ask the Assessor-Recorder for a review or file an appeal; in 2026 San Francisco's filing deadline was September 15. My report gives the board sales from your building and nearby ones, though I can't promise the outcome.

Thousand Oaks spreads across the Conejo Valley under oak-dotted hills, with 1960s and 1970s ranch homes in the older neighborhoods, planned tracts in Newbury Park, Lang Ranch and Dos Vientos, and hillside homes in North Ranch on the Westlake side. Q: We inherited a Newbury Park house that's rented out, how is it valued?

Q: Can I appeal the property tax on a Torrance house we bought at the peak?

### Ventura (https://www.cwift.net/areas/ventura)
County: Ventura County.
ZIP codes: 93001, 93003, 93004
Ventura, officially San Buenaventura, mixes beach cottages in Pierpont, older bungalows in Midtown and along the Avenue, hillside homes above downtown with ocean views, waterfront houses in the Ventura Keys, and tracts on the east end. I value homes here for probate, trusts and divorces, and since the Thomas Fire, I pay close attention to what burned, what was rebuilt and what survived.
- Hillside homes above downtown trade on the view of the ocean and the islands, so I note what you see from the main rooms, the slope, and the climb to the front door.
- In Pierpont I look at sand, salt and wind wear on the house, and whether it sits right on the beach or a few streets back, since buyers pay for every step closer.
- In the Ventura Keys I note dock size, channel frontage and seawall condition. In Midtown and on the Avenue, I look for original bungalow details and any back unit.
Photos: Photograph the ocean or island view from the main rooms, the hillside and brush clearance behind the house, and any rebuilt or new sections. Near the beach, show decks and window frames up close.
Q: Is the probate referee's value enough when we sell dad's Ventura house?
A: The referee's value serves the court inventory. For a sale, heirs often want an independent appraisal based on current Ventura sales so they can price the house and agree on any buyout. I can provide that from photos, dated to today or to the date of death.
Q: Our Ventura home was rebuilt after the Thomas Fire, how do you value it?
A: Mostly against other rebuilt homes nearby, since a new house on an old hillside lot isn't the same as one that survived. Send photos of the finishes, the systems and the yard, plus the permit or completion date, and I'll weigh the view and the brush around it.

### Vermont-Slauson / Athens, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/vermont-slauson-athens)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90044, 90047
Vermont-Slauson and Athens are blocks of small 1920s bungalows and 1940s stucco cottages off Vermont Avenue, many with a converted garage or a second unit out back. I appraise homes here for heirs who need a value as of a parent's date of death, for estates and for owners deciding whether to sell as is, and the paperwork rarely waits.
- Converted garages and back units are common here. I check the records to see which are permitted and value each part on that basis, describing anything unpermitted without counting it as legal living space.
- Original wood windows, floor furnaces and old wiring are still common in these houses. I note what's been updated from your photos, since buyers here price in whatever work is left.
- Vermont, Slauson, Manchester and Western are busy commercial streets. Homes facing them or beside a corner business sell differently from those on quieter side streets, so I use sales with the same kind of location.
Photos: Photograph the house from the street, each room, the kitchen and bath, and the floor furnace or wall heater if there is one. Show the converted garage or back unit inside and out, the electrical panel, the roof and the yard.
Q: Can you appraise my father's house in Vermont-Slauson as of when he died?
A: Yes. That's a retrospective appraisal, and it's what most estates need. I use sales from around his date of death, the county's records, and photos of the house today, adjusting if anything has changed since then. Tell me about any repairs or cleanup done after he passed.
Q: Will I get less selling my mom's house as is near Slauson?
A: Usually somewhat less than after repairs, but repairs cost money and time. My as-is appraisal compares the house with nearby sales of other unrenovated homes, so you have a realistic starting point. Whether to fix it first is between you and your agent, and I don't promise a sale price.

### Victorville (https://www.cwift.net/areas/victorville)
County: San Bernardino County.
ZIP codes: 92392, 92394, 92395
Victorville is high-desert country along the Mojave River, with older homes near the original downtown by the river, big tracts of 1980s through 2000s stucco homes west of the 15, and lake and golf-course lots in Spring Valley Lake. I value Victorville homes for estates with heirs out of state, tax appeals and sales, often on short notice.
- Spring Valley Lake homes sell apart from the rest of Victorville. I separate lakefront, golf-course and interior lots and check the HOA dues before comparing them with anything else.
- Many tract homes west of the 15 have solar panels, and I check whether they're owned or leased, since a lease changes what a buyer takes on, then compare within the same tract.
- Victor Valley sun and wind wear on stucco, roofs, windows and yards. I look closely at the roof, the AC and the yard in your photos, and I give credit for desert landscaping and covered patios.
Photos: Photograph the roof, AC unit and any solar panels, the back yard and covered patio, and the block walls. In Spring Valley Lake, show the water or golf view from the house and the path down to the lake.
Q: I inherited a house in Victorville but live back east. Can you still appraise it?
A: Yes. A property manager, agent or neighbor with a key can walk through with a phone, and I'll tell them which photos to take. I pull the county record and past MLS listings, compare the house with Victorville sales, and email you the report.
Q: Our Victorville tax bill seems too high. Can an appraisal help us appeal?
A: It can, if your Victorville home was worth less on January 1 than the county's assessed value. I appraise it as of that date using nearby Victorville sales. I give an honest value either way, and the county's appeals board decides the rest.

### Visalia (https://www.cwift.net/areas/visalia)
County: Tulare County.
ZIP codes: 93277, 93291, 93292
Visalia mixes older streets around downtown and Oval Park, postwar ranch homes under big valley oaks and newer subdivisions on the edges of town, with Mill Creek and Packwood Creek running through. I appraise homes all across Visalia for trusts, estates and divorces. You usually need the number before anything else is decided, and I start from your photos.
- Visalia's Valley Oak Ordinance protects valley oaks, so removing or pruning one involves the city. I note the trees near the house, their condition and how they limit additions, pools or driveways.
- Older homes near downtown and around Oval Park range from early 1900s houses to postwar cottages, and updates vary widely. I compare with older homes nearby, not with new tracts on the edge of town.
- Newer neighborhoods come with repeated floor plans, pools, solar and sometimes HOA dues. I compare inside the same tract, adjust for lot, plan and upgrades, and note anything behind the back fence, like a creek or canal.
Photos: Photograph any big oaks near the house and the roof under them, plus the backyard, pool, AC unit and solar. Inside, every room. If you're near Mill Creek or Packwood Creek, show what's behind the back fence.
Q: Dad's Visalia house is in a living trust, do we need an appraisal now?
A: If he has died, trustees usually want a date-of-death value to document the heirs' tax basis and to divide or sell fairly. If he's living, there's usually no need unless a transfer or gift is planned. I value the house as of whatever date the trustee or attorney names.
Q: Can you appraise my Visalia house for a past date if it's been remodeled since?
A: Yes. I appraise the house as it was on the earlier date, so I'll ask what it looked like then: the old kitchen, the roof before replacement, the room not yet added. Older photos, listing pictures or receipts help. The sales I use are from around that date.

### Vista (https://www.cwift.net/areas/vista)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 92081, 92083, 92084
Vista climbs from the old Vista Village downtown into hills planted with avocados and citrus, with 1970s and 1980s tracts in between, Shadowridge's golf course neighborhoods to the south, and larger county lots out toward Buena Creek. Heirs who live out of state often call me about a parent's place in Vista, and I work from photos someone local can take.
- Out toward Buena Creek and in other unincorporated pockets, I check for septic, a shared private road, and whether outbuildings or a second home show up in county records.
- In Shadowridge, I note golf course frontage, HOA dues and the view from the slope, then compare with resales on similar lots, fairway with fairway and street with street.
- Some hilltop homes in Vista see the ocean on clear days while neighbors downhill see rooftops, so I check what your photos show from inside and outside and compare with other view sales.
Photos: Photograph the view from the highest point of the lot and from inside, the grove and slope if you have them, and the driveway. Out toward Buena Creek, include any outbuildings, the septic area and the road in.
Q: I live in Arizona and inherited Dad's house in Vista. Do I have to come out?
A: No. A neighbor, a property manager or an agent can take photos of every room, the yard, and any grove or slope, and send them to me. I pull the records and nearby Vista sales from here, and you get the report by email, usually the next day.
Q: Should we fix the leaky roof and dead grove at Dad's Vista place before the appraisal?
A: Not for my sake. I value the house as it is, using Vista sales of homes with similar problems, and I describe the roof and the grove plainly. Whether repairs pay off before selling is a separate question, and having the as-is value first makes it easier to answer.

### West Anaheim / Stanton Border, Anaheim (https://www.cwift.net/areas/west-anaheim-stanton-border)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92804
West Anaheim, out toward the Stanton border, is mostly 1950s single-story tract houses, built in the postwar boom, on flat streets off Beach Boulevard, Brookhurst Street, Ball Road and Katella Avenue. I value homes here for estates, divorces and as-is sales, usually when someone needs a number fast, and I can do it from photos taken on your phone.
- These tracts are close cousins, so condition and upkeep separate them. I look at the roof, windows, electrical panel, kitchen and baths in your photos and compare with sales in similar shape.
- Along the Stanton border, a mailing address doesn't always tell you which city a house is in, so I confirm it from the parcel records, since local rules can differ.
- Beach Boulevard's older motels and strip centers sit right behind some backyards. I note what's over the fence and how much traffic passes, and I compare with houses in similar spots.
Photos: Photograph each room, the electrical panel, water heater and roof from the ground, and the converted garage or patio room if you have one. Show the street and what sits behind the back fence.
Q: What is a West Anaheim fixer worth before we do any repairs?
A: I value it as it stands, with photos of every problem, against sales of other fixers and dated houses nearby. That as-is number helps you decide whether to sell now, fix a few things, or let one heir buy out the others.
Q: Can you value a house as of the day my mother died last spring?
A: Yes. I use sales from around that date and the house's condition then. If you've already cleared it out or started fixing it up, send any photos from before, even phone snapshots from a family gathering, and tell me what changed.

### West LA / Sawtelle, Los Angeles (https://www.cwift.net/areas/west-la-sawtelle)
County: Los Angeles County.
ZIP codes: 90025, 90064
West LA and Sawtelle mix condo and townhome buildings around Sawtelle Boulevard and Bundy with older apartment blocks and quieter streets of 1930s and 1940s houses in Rancho Park and Cheviot Hills, all close to the 405, the 10 and the E Line. I appraise homes and condos here for estates, divorces and heir buyouts, usually on a deadline.
- Around Sawtelle and Bundy, most sales are condos and townhomes from the 1970s on. I compare within the same building or similar ones nearby and look at parking, storage, the HOA's reserves and any planned repairs.
- In Cheviot Hills and Rancho Park, 1930s and 1940s traditional and Spanish homes have often been expanded or rebuilt. I keep originals and full rebuilds apart and note any slope or view.
- Homes near the 405 and 10 interchange or beside the E Line tracks deal with noise, and a block makes a difference. I pick sales with the same exposure and note sound walls or upgraded windows in your photos.
Photos: For a condo, photograph your parking spaces and storage, the lobby or courtyard, and the view and light from each room. For a house in Cheviot Hills or Rancho Park, show the yard, any slope and added rooms.
Q: What affects the appraised value of a condo near Sawtelle Boulevard the most?
A: Size, floor and outlook come first, then parking, which matters a lot on the Westside, and the building itself: its age, amenities and finances. I weigh a building with solid reserves and no pending assessments above one facing big repairs, as buyers do.
Q: We inherited Mom's house in Cheviot Hills, how do we split it fairly?
A: Most heirs start with an independent appraisal as of the date of death, then decide whether to sell or let one person buy out the others. I compare the house with Cheviot Hills and Rancho Park sales of the same type, original or rebuilt, so the number holds up when everyone reads it.

### West Roseville / Sun City, Roseville (https://www.cwift.net/areas/west-roseville-sun-city)
County: Placer County.
ZIP codes: 95747
West Roseville and Sun City Roseville are the newer side of Roseville: single-story homes in Sun City's 55-plus community, the WestPark and Fiddyment Farm tracts, and the Sierra Vista neighborhoods rising along Fiddyment Road. Trusts, estates and Prop 19 moves bring me most of the work here, and a clear number helps everyone decide what comes next.
- Sun City Roseville homes come in a set of builder floor plans, so I match yours by model first, then adjust for golf-course frontage, lot and how much has been updated.
- WestPark and Fiddyment Farm homes often carry Mello-Roos charges and HOA dues. I note those, plus owned or leased solar, and compare with sales from the same builder era.
- Homes along Pleasant Grove Boulevard, Fiddyment Road or Blue Oaks Boulevard trade differently from interior streets. I use your photos and a map to see what's behind and beside the lot.
Photos: Photograph the kitchen, baths and great room, the patio and the view past it, solar panels, the HVAC unit, and any sunroom or patio enclosure added after the builder finished.
Q: We're moving into Sun City Roseville; can we bring our old tax base with Prop 19?
A: If you qualify, Prop 19 can let you carry your current tax base to a Sun City Roseville home, and how much carries over depends on how the two values compare. I can appraise either home as of the right dates; the assessor applies the rules.
Q: Mom's Sun City house is in her trust; does the trustee need an appraisal now?
A: Usually. The trustee needs a documented date-of-death value for basis and for dividing the trust fairly. Because Sun City Roseville has many similar floor plans selling each year, I can usually find sales of your mother's model or one very close to it.

### Western Chula Vista, Chula Vista (https://www.cwift.net/areas/western-chula-vista)
County: San Diego County.
ZIP codes: 91910, 91911
Western Chula Vista is the older part of town, between I-805 and the bay: 1920s and 1930s bungalows and Spanish-style houses near Third Avenue, then blocks of 1940s and 1950s ranch homes built as the city grew around Rohr Aircraft and the old lemon groves. I'm most often asked for a date-of-death value on these older homes, which I prepare from your photos and records.
- Between Third Avenue and I-5, I note distance to the freeway, the trolley stations at E and H Streets, and the bayfront, since each one pulls value a different way.
- The oldest houses near Third Avenue often sit on raised foundations with original wood floors and windows, so I look at foundation work, wiring and plumbing in your photos, which matter as much as a new kitchen.
- Many Rohr-era ranch houses here started small and have since grown with added bedrooms or a back unit, so I check permits and compare them with other expanded houses, not untouched originals.
Photos: Photograph the crawl space vents or foundation from outside, the wood floors and windows, and each addition or back unit, inside and out. Add the front from across the street, where its era shows.
Q: Mom died last spring. Can you value her western Chula Vista house as of that date?
A: Yes. I pick western Chula Vista sales from around that date and value the house as it was then, before any cleanout, painting or repairs, so older photos help. The estate and your CPA use that number for the step-up in basis and for dividing things among heirs.
Q: Does the rent from the back unit behind our Chula Vista house count in the appraisal?
A: Mostly through the sales. I compare your property with nearby sales of houses that also have a permitted back unit, and those prices reflect what buyers here pay for that extra income. Send the lease and photos of the unit; if it isn't permitted, the report says so and treats it conservatively.

### Willow Glen, San Jose (https://www.cwift.net/areas/willow-glen)
County: Santa Clara County.
ZIP codes: 95125
Willow Glen, once its own town southwest of downtown San Jose, has leafy streets off Lincoln Avenue with 1920s and 1930s bungalows, Spanish and Tudor cottages, postwar ranch homes and new two-stories built where small houses stood. I value homes here after a parent dies, in divorces and for trusts, often for houses held for decades, where the date-of-death value carries real tax weight.
- When a small 1920s or 1940s house sits on a good lot, buyers here may be paying mostly for the land and a chance to rebuild, so I look at teardown sales alongside remodeled ones.
- Streets matter here: a block near Lincoln Avenue or the Los Gatos Creek trail can sell differently from one beside a busy road like Curtner or Meridian, so I keep comparables close to your street.
- Palm Haven and the older streets around it have period homes with original details, and I note from your photos what's original, what's been restored and what's been replaced.
Photos: Photograph the house and lot from the street, the back yard and its trees, and the original floors, fireplace and woodwork. If a second story went on later, show the seams where it joins the original house.
Q: We need a date-of-death value for Mom's Willow Glen house for the step-up, can you?
A: Yes. I value it as of her date of death using Willow Glen sales from around then, matching age, size, lot and condition, and describe the house as it stood that day. Your CPA decides how it applies to the basis when you sell.
Q: Is our old Willow Glen house worth more as a teardown than as a home?
A: Sometimes the lot is most of the value, and I test that by comparing sales of houses bought to tear down with sales of similar homes that stayed lived in. If the teardown sales are close to or above the others, the lot is doing the work. I report the value as is either way.

### Yorba Linda (https://www.cwift.net/areas/yorba-linda)
County: Orange County.
ZIP codes: 92886, 92887
Yorba Linda, home of the Nixon Library, has 1960s and 1970s ranch homes on big lots laced with horse trails, two-story tracts from the 1980s and 1990s, and newer hillside streets near Black Gold golf course. I value homes here for trusts, divorces and buyouts, usually with a date to meet, and the outdoor features count as much as the rooms.
- Horse-zoned lots with trail access are their own market. I note the barn, arena, corrals, trail gate and usable flat land, and compare with other horse properties rather than standard tracts.
- The 2008 Freeway Complex Fire burned into Yorba Linda's hills, so for hillside homes I look at rebuilt versus original houses, brush clearance, slope and the view.
- In East Lake Village and other HOA tracts, I note dues and any lake or clubhouse rights, and compare inside the same community before looking farther out.
Photos: Photograph the barn, arena, corrals and trail gate if you have them, the slope and brush behind the house, the view from the back yard, and inside, the kitchen and baths.
Q: In our divorce, does the appraisal count that my parents helped buy the house?
A: No. The appraisal gives the market value of the house as of the date your attorneys need, nothing more. Who contributed what is for your attorneys, a mediator or the court to sort out. I stay neutral and value the house the same way no matter which side orders.
Q: How fast can you appraise a Yorba Linda home for a trust?
A: I email it within 24 hours of payment and photos, any day of the week. Trust work often has a trustee waiting to act, so send everything at once: every room, the yard, and any barn, arena or view that matters to the value.

### Yucaipa (https://www.cwift.net/areas/yucaipa)
County: San Bernardino County.
ZIP codes: 92399
Yucaipa sits against the foothills below the San Bernardino Mountains, with San Gorgonio and Yucaipa Ridge behind it. Homes range from older ranch houses on big lots and horse properties to newer tracts, hillside homes with long views, and several 55-plus mobile home communities. I value Yucaipa homes when a parent's house passes to the kids, for estates and before a sale, usually on a deadline.
- Views of San Gorgonio and the valley carry real weight on Yucaipa's hillside streets. I judge how open the view is and how usable the lot is, and compare with sales that have similar views.
- Many Yucaipa lots are large, with horse setups, fruit trees, workshops and RV parking. I compare them with other big-lot sales, because they don't trade like the newer tracts.
- The canyons above town toward Oak Glen burned in the 2020 El Dorado Fire. I note brush clearance, the roof and the road in from your photos, and compare with homes that share the same fire exposure.
Photos: Photograph the mountain view from the yard, the slope and brush around the lot, and any barn, corral or workshop. Show the fruit trees, the RV gate, and the kitchen and baths, whether original or redone.
Q: Do we need to clean out Mom's Yucaipa house before you appraise it?
A: No. I value the Yucaipa house, not the furniture, so photos with her things still in place work fine. Just make sure each room shows its floors, walls and ceilings, and include the yard, the view and any workshop or barn. I compare it with sales on similar lots nearby.
Q: Can you appraise a Yucaipa property with a second house or granny flat?
A: Yes. I value the main house and second unit together and compare with Yucaipa and Redlands sales that also have one. Permits, a separate meter and a private entry all matter, so send photos of both units and any permit paperwork.
